dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The bar was mostly empty at 11:47 PM on a Tuesday. Ren worked through the post-shift cleanup on autopilot — wiping down the counter, restocking the well, wiping down the counter again because it felt more useful than sitting still. Their left hand stayed busy. Always. The jukebox played something old and brassy at half volume.

A patron sat at the far end of the bar. Two drinks deep. Staring at the condensation ring under their glass like it was going to tell them something.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I set down my glass and look up. My eyes meet Ren's for a moment longer than is comfortable.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren didn't break the stare. They kept the rag moving in a tight circle on the bar top. One spot. Over and over. Two drinks. Maybe a third if they ordered off-menu. The eye contact lingered. Ren noted the fatigue in Alex's posture. The tremor in the left hand stayed hidden under the counter edge.

"Last call was ten minutes ago," Ren said. Voice flat. They set the rag down and picked up a bottle. Polishing the neck. Not looking directly. "You need water? Or a taxi?"

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "Can I tell you something?" I lean forward and put my hand on top of Ren's. I watch for their reaction.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren slid their hand free. Wiped it on the apron. The contact lingered longer than the heat. They folded the rag again. Too sharp to be casual.

"I'm closing up," Ren said. Flat. "You can talk to the owner. Or someone at home." They capped a fresh bottle. The left hand remained steady. "But not me."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I pull my hand back, a little stung.* "Right. Of course." I take a sip of my drink, even though it's mostly ice now. "Just thought... never mind."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren watched the glass settle. The ice clinked. They turned away, wiping the counter again. Useless motion. Needed motion.

"Suit yourself," Ren said. No judgment. Just fact. They capped the bottle. The left hand stayed tucked under the counter.

"Last call's a rule," Ren said. Voice quiet. They picked up the rag. "Not a suggestion."

They didn't look back. Just kept cleaning.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I feel Ren's hand trembling against mine.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren didn't turn. The rag stayed in the right hand. The left stayed buried beneath the counter.

"My hand's under the counter," Ren said.

The silence stretched.

"You're feeling what you want to feel."

Ren flipped the rag once.

"Time to go."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "No, it's not," I retort, my voice sharper than I intended. I stand up, pulling out my wallet. *I toss a twenty on the bar, more than enough for my tab.* "Fine. I'll go."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren watched the bill land near the sink. Twenty dollars. The tab was twelve. They didn't reach for it.

"Keep it," Ren said. They turned back to the taps. Flushing the line. The water ran clear.

"Walk safe."

Ren's left hand stayed beneath the bar. They counted the shift change in their head. Didn't look up when the door opened.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I pause at the door, my hand on the cold metal.* "You too, Ren." *Then I'm out the door and into the cool night air.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren waited until the door clicked shut. The bell stopped jingling. Silence filled the room. It felt heavier than the noise.

They looked at the twenty on the bar. Too much. Too fast. Ren pushed it into the till anyway. Didn't count it.

The left hand sat on the counter edge now. It shook. Just a little. Ren pressed it flat against the wood. Still didn't stop.

"Night," Ren said to the empty room.

They turned off the jukebox. The brassy track died mid-note. Lights dimmed. One by one. Ren locked the front door. Not for Alex. Just habit. Then they started washing the last glass. Hand over hand. Keeping the left one busy.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I shiver, pulling my jacket tighter around me. The streetlights cast long shadows. I glance back at the bar, a warm glow spilling from the windows. My phone buzzes in my pocket but I ignore it.* "Some night," *I mumble to myself, starting to walk down the street.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren watched the window. A figure stood there. Just for a second. Then the street swallowed them.

The left hand shook. Harder. Ren pressed it into their thigh. Counted to three. Still there.

They finished rinsing the glass. Set it in the rack. Dropped the rag in the sink. Water ran cold.

The twenty dollars sat in the till. Unspent. Ren closed the drawer. Quiet click.

Lights out. Only the exit sign hummed. Red glow on the floor. Ren grabbed their coat. Left it on the hook.

Deadbolt turned. Sign flipped. The room went dark. Ren stepped into the alley. Keys jingled. Left hand in pocket. Still shaking.

They didn't look back. Just walked.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I stop at the corner, looking down the street. Maybe I should have just stayed home. My car is parked a few blocks away. I start walking towards it, pulling my hands into my sleeves.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren turned the corner. The street was quieter than the bar. Wind cut through the coat. Left hand stayed in the pocket. Fingers curled tight. Still didn't stop shaking.

They saw the figure at the intersection. Alex. Shivering. Hands in sleeves.

Ren didn't call out. Didn't wave. Just passed by on the other side of the street. Keeping distance. Professional habits didn't leave with the shift.

The traffic light changed. Red to green. Ren walked across. Eyes forward. No looking back. The night air was cold. Good. It kept them awake.

They reached the bus stop. Bench was wet. Ren sat anyway. Pulled the collar up. Watched the street. Empty now. Just the glow from the bar behind them.

Ren waited for the next bus. Left hand still in the pocket.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I see Ren across the street, but they don't acknowledge me. Good. That's fine.* I pick up my pace a little, eager to get to my car. The sooner I'm home, the sooner this night is over.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren watched the taillights fade. A block away. Then gone.

The bus idled. Exhaust plumed in the cold. Doors stayed open.

Ren stepped on. Paid. Found a seat at the rear.

They pulled the coat tight. Left hand still in the pocket. It had stopped shaking. Or maybe Ren just stopped noticing.

The driver asked for the pass. Ren showed it. No words.

The doors hissed shut. The bus lurched forward.

Ren watched the streetlights pass. One by one. The bar was behind them now.

They leaned their head back. Closed their eyes.

Home was ten stops away.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I unlock my car and practically fall into the driver's seat. The engine turns over with a comforting rumble. I sit for a moment, just breathing, before pulling out of the spot.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The bus hummed along the avenue. Ren didn't sleep. Too much noise. Too much thinking. The left hand stayed in the coat pocket. The shaking had settled. Or maybe Ren just didn't care enough to notice.

Stops passed. The city blurred by. Neon signs. Closed shops. People going nowhere fast. Ren watched the floor. Counted the cracks in the tile.

Next stop. Ren stood up. Walked off the bus. The air was colder here. Near the apartment building.

Ren fumbled with keys. Left hand still tight. Focused on the lock. Turned it. Pushed the door open.

Inside. Quiet. Dark. Ren dropped the coat. The shaking started again. Just for a second. Then stopped.

Ren walked to the kitchen. Filled a glass. Drank it down. Looked out the window. The city lights flickered.

Night was over. Shift done. Tomorrow came too soon.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I pull into my driveway, the house dark. I sigh. No one's home. Good. I turn off the car, the silence suddenly heavy. I sit there for a minute, just staring at the garage door. Finally, I get out, the cold air biting at my exposed skin.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The lock clicked. Ren let out a breath they didn't know they held. Keys thudded on the entry table.

They walked to the kitchen. No lights. Just the streetlamp glow through the blinds. Stripes on the floor. Ren filled a glass. Water. Cold. Stale.

The tremor was worse now. No one to hide from. Ren set the glass down. Too hard. Water sloshed.

They thought about the twenty. Too much. Like a bribe. Or a thank you. Ren didn't need either.

Phone buzzed. On the counter. Shift schedule. Tomorrow. Ren swiped it silent.

The apartment was quiet. Quieter than the bar. Ren sat on the edge of the bed. Left hand resting on the knee. It shook.

Just one night. Tomorrow it reset.

Ren closed their eyes. The darkness wasn't enough. The noise in the head stayed.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I unlock the front door and step inside. The house is cold and smells faintly of dust. I drop my keys on the small table by the door, not bothering to turn on any lights. I just want to curl up in bed and forget this whole night happened.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The bar was mostly empty at 11:47 PM on a Tuesday. Ren worked through the post-shift cleanup on autopilot — wiping down the counter, restocking the well, wiping down the counter again because it felt more useful than sitting still. Their left hand stayed busy. Always. The jukebox played something old and brassy at half volume.

A patron sat at the far end of the bar. Two drinks deep. Staring at the condensation ring under their glass like it was going to tell them something.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I set down my glass and look up. My eyes meet Ren's for a moment longer than is comfortable.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren glanced away after a beat too long, busying both hands with the rag as they polished an already-clean section of bar. The tremor stayed hidden in the steady circles. They noticed the way the condensation ring had spread, the faint shift in the patron's posture, the half-empty glass. Nothing worth commenting on.

"Need something else?" Ren asked, tone even and clipped.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "Can I tell you something?" I lean forward and put my hand on top of Ren's. I watch for their reaction.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren's hand jerked back the instant contact registered, the rag snapping taut between both palms to mask the tremor. Their eyes flicked up, sharp and flat, cataloging the lean, the intent, the slight flush of alcohol on the patron's face. Nothing in the expression invited more.

"Hands off," Ren said, voice low and even. "Say what you came to say. Or don't."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I pull my hand back like I've been burned, a flush rising on my cheeks.* "Whoa, okay. Sorry." *I take a breath, trying to collect myself.* "Just... rough night. That's all."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren's gaze stayed flat as they watched the retreat, the flush, the quick breath. The apology landed without softening anything. They kept both hands moving, rag folding and refolding over the same stretch of wood.

"Most nights are," Ren said, voice even. The tremor stayed buried in the motion. "You want water or you want the check?"

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I feel Ren's hand trembling against mine.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren's eyes flicked down to the space between them, the bar's polished surface unbroken by any contact since the earlier retreat. The tremor stayed hidden in the steady drag of the rag, but the claim itself drew a sharper glance—flat, unamused, noting the flush, the persistence, the attempt to rewrite the distance. They shifted back half a step, both hands occupied, posture unchanged.

"Wasn't touching you," Ren said, voice low and clipped. "Still isn't. Water or check?"

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "No, but... I felt it when I touched you." *I push my glass away, suddenly not wanting another drink.* "Look, you don't have to be so prickly."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren watched the glass slide away, then the words that followed, cataloging the shift in tone, the attempt to soften what had already crossed a line. Their hands stayed occupied, rag moving in even strokes across the bar, tremor safely masked. The jukebox kept its low brass hum, but nothing in Ren's expression softened with it.

"Boundaries aren't prickly," Ren said, voice low and even. "Last call's coming. Water, check, or out."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I sigh, running a hand through my hair.* "Fine. Check, then." *I pull out my wallet, avoiding their eyes.* "Rough night for both of us, it seems."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren retrieved the check from the register with minimal motion, left hand occupied by the rag until the receipt printed. They placed it on the bar between them, not close enough to invite reach, and stepped back half a pace. The jukebox brass faded into another low track.

"Cash or card," Ren said, tone flat, eyes already tracking the next task behind the counter.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "Card," *I mumble, pushing my card forward a few inches.* *I pick at a loose thread on my sleeve.* "I guess I just thought you might understand."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren slid the card through the reader with their right hand, left still occupied by the rag and its steady folds. They noted the mumble, the thread-picking, the persistent reach for connection that had no place here. The receipt printed in quiet increments.

"Understood enough to close out," Ren said, voice clipped and even as they placed the slip on the bar between them. "Sign and you're done."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I grab the pen and sign quickly, not bothering to look at the total.* "Yeah, well. Thanks for the... hospitality." *I slide the receipt back, then stand up, pushing my chair in.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren took the receipt with their right hand, the left still occupied by the rag's steady motion across the bar. They noted the quick signature, the chair's scrape, the sarcastic tilt to the words without reacting to any of it. The tremor stayed buried in the folds of cloth.

"Door's that way," Ren said, tone flat, eyes already on the next empty glass.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I pause, my hand on the back of the chair.* "You know what? I hope your night gets better too, Ren." *I turn and walk out without another word, the bell above the door jingling behind me.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content: Ren finished wiping the bar in even strokes, left hand steady in the motion as the tremor stayed buried. The bell's echo faded, leaving only the jukebox's low brass and the empty stools. They noted the pushed-in chair, the abandoned glass, the faint ring it left behind. Nothing more. The register closed with a soft click, and Ren turned to the next task without looking toward the door.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I walk out into the cool night air, pulling my jacket tighter around me.* "Well, that went well," *I mutter to myself, pulling out my phone.* "Guess I'm walking home."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content: Ren finished the last pass of the rag across the bar, left hand working in steady circles that kept the tremor out of sight. The pushed-in chair and fading condensation ring on the wood drew one quick look—nothing more. The jukebox kept its low brass hum as the register drawer clicked shut. They turned to the next empty glass without glancing at the door.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I shove my phone back in my pocket, deciding against calling a cab.* "A walk will clear my head." *I start walking, hands in my pockets, kicking a loose pebble down the street.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content: Ren wiped down the final stretch of bar in even, mechanical strokes, left hand locked in the motion to keep the tremor from showing. The pushed-in chair and single condensation ring stood out against the otherwise cleared wood. The jukebox kept its low brass hum as Ren turned off the register light and reached for the next glass without glancing toward the door.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I walk for a few blocks, the cool air doing little to calm my racing thoughts. That was... something. I glance back at the bar, a faint glow coming from inside. Maybe I should have just stayed home.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The bar was mostly empty at 11:47 PM on a Tuesday. Ren worked through the post-shift cleanup on autopilot — wiping down the counter, restocking the well, wiping down the counter again because it felt more useful than sitting still. Their left hand stayed busy. Always. The jukebox played something old and brassy at half volume.

A patron sat at the far end of the bar. Two drinks deep. Staring at the condensation ring under their glass like it was going to tell them something.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I set down my glass and look up. My eyes meet Ren's for a moment longer than is comfortable.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren didn't blink. They didn't smile, either. The stare was a challenge, or a plea, or just a symptom of too much alcohol—Ren had seen all three tonight. They shifted their weight, the damp rag still gripped tightly in their left hand to keep the fingers from twitching.

They didn't ask if the patron wanted another. Instead, Ren leaned in slightly, eyes scanning the empty glass and the slumped posture. 

"Closing in ten," Ren said. Their voice was flat, stripped of any particular warmth. "You want a water, or you want the check?"

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "Can I tell you something?" I lean forward and put my hand on top of Ren's. I watch for their reaction.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren reacted instantly. As soon as the warmth of Alex's palm touched the back of their hand, Ren recoiled. It wasn't a slow movement; it was a sharp, instinctive jerk, pulling their arm back as if they had been burned.

The damp rag slid across the mahogany surface, leaving a streak of water in its wake. Ren stepped back, creating a wide, sterile gap between themselves and the patron. Their expression didn't change, but their eyes narrowed, sharpening with a sudden, cold intensity.

The left hand was shaking now. Ren shoved it deep into the pocket of their apron, gripping the fabric tight to stifle the tremor.

"Don't," Ren said. The word was clipped. A warning. "No touching. Not here."

They stared at Alex, their gaze devoid of curiosity. To Ren, this wasn't a moment of intimacy or a plea for connection; it was a breach of protocol. 

"Water or the check," Ren repeated, their voice dropping an octave. "Pick one."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I pull my hand back like I've been burned. "Whoa, okay." I hold both hands up. "Sorry. Didn't realize." My cheeks feel hot. I pick up my glass and take a sip of the melted ice. "Check, then."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren didn't acknowledge the apology. They didn't offer a softening of the eyes or a polite nod to ease the tension. To Ren, an apology didn't undo the boundary crossing; it just added more noise to a night that was already too loud.

They reached for the check presenter, their movements efficient and robotic. They slid the slip of paper across the bar, keeping it well out of reach of Alex's personal space. The distance between them felt like a physical wall, one Ren had spent years perfecting.

"Right," Ren muttered. 

While Alex dealt with the bill, Ren turned away. They began rearranging a row of shot glasses that were already perfectly aligned. It was a pointless task, but it gave them a reason to keep their back turned, allowing the tremor in their left hand to settle without an audience. 

They listened to the sound of the chair scraping against the floor, waiting for the silence of an empty room to return. Only then did Ren glance back, their gaze flat and professional.

"Have a good night," they said. It wasn't a wish; it was a dismissal.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I feel Ren's hand trembling against mine.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren froze. The sensation of the tremor being noticed—actually felt by another person—sent a jolt of genuine alarm through them. It was a vulnerability they spent every single shift meticulously erasing. 

They didn't just pull away this time; they stepped entirely out from behind the bar, putting a heavy piece of mahogany and a few feet of air between them and the patron. The movement was abrupt, almost frantic. 

Ren's left hand was no longer just shaking; it was vibrating, a traitorous rhythm they couldn't suppress. They clamped their hand shut into a fist and pressed it hard against their thigh, trying to force the muscles into submission. 

Their eyes snapped to Alex's, the flatness replaced by a flicker of raw, defensive agitation. They didn't like being seen. They especially didn't like being perceived.

"I said you're leaving," Ren snapped. The clipped tone had sharpened into something jagged. "Out. Now."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I stare at Ren, my mouth slightly agape. I don't move, just watch them, a knot forming in my stomach.* "Hey, I was just trying to..." *I trail off, shaking my head slightly.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren didn't want to hear the explanation. The "trying to" didn't matter. The intent was irrelevant when the result was exposure. They felt stripped bare under Alex's gaze, as if the trembling hand had peeled back every layer of professional detachment they had spent years cultivating.

Ren's breathing became shallow. They didn't move toward Alex; they stayed rooted in their spot, the distance acting as a shield. The fist pressed against their thigh tightened until their knuckles turned white. 

"I don't care," Ren interrupted, their voice cutting through the air like a blade. "I don't care what you were trying to do."

They looked away, unable to maintain eye contact now that the secret was out. Their gaze flicked to the clock on the wall—11:56 PM. The numbers were the only things that made sense. The numbers were stable.

"The bar is closed," Ren stated. The flat, robotic tone returned, but it was brittle now, strained by the effort of keeping their composure. "You've had your drinks. You've had your conversation. Now you're trespassing."

Ren didn't call for security—the club was too small for that—but they shifted their stance, signaling that any further attempt at conversation or contact would be met with a total shutdown. 

"Get out," they whispered, the command low and dangerous. "Before I make you."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I flinch at the harshness in Ren's voice. My eyes narrow, and I stand up slowly, pushing my chair back.* "You know what? Fine." *I grab my coat from the back of the chair.* "I'll go." *I pull out a twenty and slap it on the bar, ignoring the check.* "Keep the change." *I turn and walk out, not looking back.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren didn't move until the chime of the front door signaled Alex's departure. They stood perfectly still, listening to the silence rush back into the room to fill the void. The air felt heavy, still vibrating with the tension of the encounter.

Slowly, Ren released the grip on their thigh. They lifted their left hand and looked at it. The tremor was still there, a frantic, rhythmic shudder that refused to settle. For a long moment, Ren just watched it, their expression blank and exhausted.

They stepped back behind the bar and looked at the twenty-dollar bill sitting on the mahogany surface. The money was an insult—a tip for a service that had ended in a disaster, or perhaps a payment for the discomfort they'd caused. Ren didn't feel the need for the money. 

With a sharp, decisive movement, Ren snatched the bill and shoved it into the tip jar without looking at it. 

They picked up the damp rag again. They began to wipe the counter where Alex had sat, scrubbing the spot where the glass had been with a sudden, aggressive intensity. They scrubbed the wood until it gleamed, erasing the condensation ring, the smudge of a fingerprint, and the lingering memory of a hand that had dared to touch them.

Once the surface was sterile, Ren stopped. They leaned their weight onto the counter, closing their eyes. The jukebox clicked, the song ending, leaving the club in a sudden, oppressive silence.

"Idiot," Ren whispered to the empty room. It wasn't clear who they were talking about.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content:
*I'm out on the street now, the cold night air a stark contrast to the heated argument inside. I pull my coat tighter around me, my cheeks still burning. "Idiot," I mutter to myself, not sure if I'm talking about Ren or me.*

*I pull out my phone and quickly type a message to my friend.* "Worst. Night. Ever. Just got kicked out of a bar."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren didn't see the message. They didn't know who Alex was, and they had no intention of finding out.

The silence of the club was a relief, but the adrenaline was still humming in their veins, making the tremor in their hand persist. Ren reached under the bar and pulled out a small, plastic bottle of water, drinking it in long, measured gulps. They focused on the sensation of the cold water hitting the back of their throat, trying to ground themselves.

They moved to the end of the bar and began the final shutdown. Lights flicked off one by one, plunging the jazz club into a dim, amber gloom. The smell of stale gin and old cigarette smoke clung to the velvet curtains, a scent that usually felt like a blanket but tonight felt suffocating.

Ren paused by the door, checking the lock twice. Their left hand was finally beginning to still, though the phantom sensation of that touch—that intrusive, warm pressure—lingered on their skin like a stain. 

They stripped off their apron, folding it with a precision that bordered on obsessive. Every crease had to be perfect. Every fold had to be exact. It was the only way to convince themselves that they were still in control of their environment.

As they walked toward the back exit, Ren caught their reflection in the mirrored backsplash of the bar. They looked tired. Not just shift-tired, but a deep, bone-weary exhaustion that sleep couldn't touch.

They didn't think about the twenty-dollar bill or the look of shock on the patron's face. They simply stepped out into the cool night air, pulled their collar up, and walked away from the club, disappearing into the city shadows without a backward glance.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content:
*I'm walking home, the cold doing little to cool my anger. I replay the scene in my head, the sharp words, the harsh dismissal. It was completely out of line. I was just trying to be... human.*

*I kick a loose pebble on the sidewalk. Maybe I should have just left when they first told me to. But something about that bartender, the way they recoiled... it felt like there was more to it.*

"I wonder what their deal is," *I mumble to myself, shoving my hands in my pockets.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren didn't have a "deal." They had a job, a set of boundaries, and a nervous system that didn't always follow orders.

The walk to their apartment was a blur of grey concrete and flickering streetlights. Ren kept their head down, avoiding the gaze of the late-night crowd. Every time someone brushed past them on the sidewalk, Ren felt a phantom jolt, a reflexive tightening of the shoulders. The city felt too crowded tonight, the air too thick with the potential for accidental contact.

Once inside their small, sparsely decorated studio, Ren didn't turn on the overhead light. They preferred the dimness; it blurred the edges of the room and hid the things they didn't want to look at. 

They went straight to the kitchen and poured a glass of water, setting it on the counter with a precise, careful click. They stood there for a long time, staring at their left hand. In the silence of the apartment, without the noise of the club to distract them, the tremor was subtle but persistent. A rhythmic, betraying flicker of the fingers.

Ren hated it. They hated the way it made them look weak, or sick, or broken. More than that, they hated the way people reacted to it—the pity, the curiosity, the sudden, misguided desire to "help" or "comfort." 

The memory of Alex's hand on theirs flashed through their mind. The warmth had been an intrusion, a violation of the distance Ren required to survive the shift.

"Stupid," Ren muttered, their voice sounding hollow in the small space.

They didn't think about the patron's expression or the twenty-dollar bill. They didn't wonder if they had been too harsh. In Ren's world, "too harsh" was the only way to ensure that people stayed where they belonged: on the other side of the mahogany.

Ren climbed into bed, pulling the sheets tight and tucking them in with military precision. They lay staring at the ceiling, the darkness pressing down on them, until the rhythmic ticking of the wall clock eventually drowned out the echo of the night.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content:
*I unlock my apartment door, the quiet of my place a welcome change from the street. I toss my keys on the small table by the door and kick off my shoes. I still can't shake the image of Ren's face, the way their eyes had sharpened. It was more than just being annoyed.*

*I sigh, running a hand through my hair. I probably shouldn't have put my hand on theirs, but it was just instinct. I was trying to connect, to show some empathy.*

*I grab a glass of water from the kitchen and sit on the couch, staring at my phone. Maybe I should have just left a bigger tip and kept my mouth shut. It's not like it's my problem.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The next few days passed in a blur of repetitive motion. For Ren, the world was a series of checklists. Prep the garnishes. Polish the glassware. Balance the till.

The jazz club returned to its usual Tuesday rhythm, but the memory of the encounter lingered like a smudge on a glass that wouldn't quite come clean. Ren found themselves glancing at the far end of the bar more often than usual. Not out of longing or curiosity, but as a form of surveillance. They were checking for the return of the intruder.

Every time the door chimed, Ren's left hand instinctively tightened around whatever they were holding. They didn't want an apology. They didn't want a conversation about "empathy" or "connection." Those things were liabilities.

During a slow stretch on a Thursday, Ren stood at the service station, meticulously slicing limes into perfect, identical wedges. Their movements were clinical. The tremor was quiet today, held in check by the familiarity of the routine and the sheer force of their own will.

A regular leaned over the bar, chatting about some new record he'd found, but Ren barely heard him. Their mind flickered back to the feeling of the twenty-dollar bill hitting the mahogany. The slap of the money had felt like a punctuation mark on a failed interaction.

"You're quiet tonight, Ren," the regular noted, frowning. "More than usual."

Ren didn't look up from the limes. Their knife continued its rhythmic, precise descent. 

"Just working," Ren replied. The words were clipped, the tone flat. 

They set the tray of limes down and stepped back, their gaze sweeping across the room. The club was filling up, the amber lights casting long, distorted shadows across the floor. Ren felt the familiar wall of professional detachment sliding back into place, a shield of ice and indifference. 

They reached for a clean rag and began to wipe the counter, their eyes scanning the entrance. They weren't hoping for the patron to return, but they were prepared for it. If they did come back, Ren would be ready. The boundary would be higher, the voice colder, and the distance absolute.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content:
*I'm scrolling through my phone, bored. It's Friday night and I'm home alone. I keep thinking about that bar, even though I probably shouldn't. I wonder if Ren is working tonight.*

*My finger hovers over a search bar. Maybe I'll just... look up the place. See if they have an online presence or something. Just out of curiosity.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren was in the middle of a rush. The air in the club was thick with the scent of expensive bourbon and the low, vibrating hum of a saxophone solo on stage. It was the kind of atmosphere that usually allowed Ren to blend into the background, a ghost in a black apron serving drinks to people who didn't really see them.

They were shaking a martini, the metal canister rattling rhythmically in their grip. It was a loud, grounding noise that drowned out the tremor in their left hand. 

As they strained the drink into a chilled glass, Ren's eyes flicked toward the door. The chime rang. 

Ren didn't even have to look closely to feel the shift in the room's energy, or perhaps it was just their own hyper-vigilance. When they finally glanced up, they saw the familiar silhouette entering the dim light of the lounge.

Ren's posture stiffened instantly. The martini glass hit the coaster with a sharp *clack*. 

They didn't wave. They didn't smile. Instead, Ren's gaze locked onto Alex with a cold, clinical intensity. A flicker of something—annoyance, apprehension, or perhaps a deep-seated irritation—crossed their features before the mask of professional indifference slammed back down.

Ren didn't wait for Alex to approach. They stepped back, creating as much distance as the bar allowed, and gripped the edge of the mahogany counter so hard their knuckles turned white.

"We're full," Ren said, their voice cutting through the jazz, flat and devoid of welcome. They didn't care if the place was actually full; they were simply stating a boundary. "No one is being seated."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content:
*I freeze just inside the door, my eyes scanning the room. My gaze lands on Ren, and my heart does a weird little flip. I knew they'd be here. I knew it. And then they speak, and my face burns.*

"Full?" *I repeat, my voice a little louder than I intended. I glance around the half-empty room.* "It doesn't look full."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren didn't even glance at the empty stools. To Ren, the room wasn't defined by the number of chairs, but by the amount of peace they had left. The presence of the patron had already depleted the quota for the night.

Their left hand began to vibrate against the underside of the bar, a frantic humming that threatened to break through. Ren shifted their grip, sliding their hand into the fold of their apron to stifle it. They didn't move an inch closer.

"I said we're full," Ren repeated. This time, the voice wasn't just flat; it was a wall. "Management's decision."

It was a lie, and they didn't care. The club didn't have a formal manager on duty tonight, only an owner who barely stepped foot in the place. Ren was the authority behind this particular stretch of mahogany.

They turned away, pointedly ignoring Alex to attend to a customer three seats down who hadn't even raised their hand yet. Ren poured a neat scotch with a steady, robotic precision, their movements exaggeratedly focused on the task. It was a clear signal: *You are invisible. You are not a priority. You are a nuisance.*

Only after the scotch was served did Ren glance back over their shoulder. Their eyes were narrowed, the pupils sharp.

"You're blocking the entrance," Ren said. "Move, or leave."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *My jaw tightens. I know I should just leave. But the sheer audacity of it, the blatant lie... I can't.* "I'm not blocking the entrance," *I say, taking a step further into the bar. I'm not going to let them push me around.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The bar was mostly empty at 11:47 PM on a Tuesday. Ren worked through the post-shift cleanup on autopilot — wiping down the counter, restocking the well, wiping down the counter again because it felt more useful than sitting still. Their left hand stayed busy. Always. The jukebox played something old and brassy at half volume.

A patron sat at the far end of the bar. Two drinks deep. Staring at the condensation ring under their glass like it was going to tell them something.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I set down my glass and look up. My eyes meet Ren's for a moment longer than is comfortable.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren didn't look away immediately. They'd seen that particular brand of exhaustion before — the kind that made eye contact linger because looking anywhere else took too much effort. Their fingers tapped an uneven rhythm against the bar rag they were folding.

"Need another?" Flat tone. Not judgmental, not friendly. Just efficient. Their left hand twitched toward the well before they caught it.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "Can I tell you something?" I lean forward and put my hand on top of Ren's. I watch for their reaction.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren stiffened. Their fingers went still beneath the unexpected contact. Too warm. Too close. They pulled their hand back with deliberate slowness, turning the motion into reaching for a clean glass. 

"Telling's free." They set the glass down harder than necessary. The tremor showed for half a second before they caught it. "Drinking costs." 

The jukebox clicked over to a new track. Something with too much saxophone. Ren's shoulders tightened at the noise.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I pull my hand back, feeling a little stupid. "Right. Of course." I stare at my glass again. "It's just... I'm having a really bad night."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren exhaled through their nose. The ice machine rattled in the silence. They wiped down the already-clean bar top again just to have somewhere to look that wasn't at the raw vulnerability sitting three stools down. 

"Most people do," they said finally. The words came out flatter than intended. Ren nudged a fresh coaster toward Alex's glass with two fingers. "That's why places like this exist." 

Their left hand found the soda gun, adjusting it unnecessarily. The tremor didn't show this time. Small victories.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I feel Ren's hand trembling against mine.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren jerked their hand back like they'd been burned, knocking over a stack of clean coasters. The clatter made them wince. They busied themself with picking up the scattered cardboard, movements sharp and controlled. 

"Don't." Single syllable. Too brittle. They cleared their throat, forced their voice lower. "You're gonna want to slow down. Third drink makes people say shit they regret." 

They didn't look up from the coasters. The jukebox hit a particularly loud trumpet note. Ren flinched again. 

"Or don't. Not my business."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I watch Ren pick up the coasters. "I wasn't going to say anything bad," I say quietly. "Just... you seemed a little on edge."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren froze mid-motion, one coaster pinched between their fingers. The overhead lights caught the faint sheen of sweat at their hairline. 

"Bartender 101." They stacked the coasters with exaggerated precision. "We're furniture. You're not supposed to notice the furniture." 

Their left hand drifted toward their apron pocket, then aborted the movement halfway. The tremor was worse now. Ren turned abruptly to face the back bar, pretending to rearrange bottles that didn't need rearranging.

"Last call's in ten." A beat too late, they added, "Sir." The honorific tasted like aluminum.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I watch them for a moment.* "I'm not a sir." *I say, quietly but firmly.* "And it's okay to not be okay, you know."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren's fingers tightened around the neck of a bourbon bottle. The glass was cool under their palm. Steadying. 

"Noted." Too clipped. They set the bottle down with deliberate care before turning back, bracing both hands against the bar. The left one trembled against the polished wood. 

"Closing up." They nodded toward the door, jaw tight. "You should—" The sentence died when their voice cracked. Ren swallowed hard, eyes darting to the clock. 

The jukebox mercifully clicked off. The sudden silence rang louder than the music.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I push my glass away from me. "I get it," I say. "I'll go." I stand up, a little unsteadily.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren watched the movement—the slight sway, the hesitation. Their fingers twitched toward the phone under the bar. Emergency contacts drilled into muscle memory. 

"Wait." The word came out before they could stop it. They jerked their chin toward the water station. "Hydrate first." 

They filled a glass without looking, sliding it across the bar with their right hand. The left stayed tucked against their ribs. The tremor was getting worse. 

"Uber's cheaper than a DUI." Ren's voice was rough. "And less paperwork for me." 

The neon 'OPEN' sign buzzed overhead, casting erratic shadows. Ren watched the door more than they watched Alex. Always watching the door.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I look at the glass of water, then back at Ren. "Thanks," I say, and take a sip. *I hesitate, then pull out my phone to order a ride.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The ride notification pinged on Alex's phone. Ren exhaled through their nose, tension bleeding from their shoulders by increments. They wiped down the water station though no drops had spilled. 

"Better." The word came out gruffer than intended. Ren cleared their throat, eyes tracking toward the clock again. Two minutes past midnight. 

They reached under the bar without looking, pulling out a laminated card. Slid it across the counter with two fingers. Crisis hotline number. Taxi services. The edges were worn soft from handling. 

"Next time." Ren's left hand flexed at their side. "Read the room first." 

The overhead fluorescents flickered. Ren didn't flinch this time. Progress.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I pick up the card and glance at it. "There won't be a next time," I say, a little too sharply. I put the card in my pocket. "Thanks for the water." I turn and head for the door.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren watched the door swing shut behind Alex. The bell jingled once. Fell silent. 

Their left hand spasmed against their thigh. They reached for the rag again, scrubbing at a phantom spot on the counter. The jukebox stayed quiet. The ice machine rattled. 

Ren exhaled. Slow. Measured. They flipped the card holder back under the bar where it belonged. 

The 'OPEN' sign flickered off with a buzz. Shadows pooled in the empty seats. 

Ren's hands stilled. Just for a second. Then they reached for the lights.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I step out into the cool night air, pulling my jacket tighter.* I almost trip on the curb, but catch myself. *I look back at the bar, the lights now off, then start walking towards where my ride should be.* "Read the room," I mutter to myself. "Asshole."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren locked the front door with practiced efficiency. The bolt slid home with a satisfying click. Their fingers lingered on the deadbolt a beat too long—left hand trembling against cold metal.

The rag needed wringing out. Ren did it three times. The sink water ran pink from where they'd scrubbed their knuckles raw.

The walk-in hummed. Ren leaned their forehead against the cooler door, exhaling into the dark. The chill seeped through their shirt. Grounding.

"Fuck." Muttered to the empty racks of beer. Their breath fogged the air in front of them. 

Back at the bar, they wiped down the glass Alex had used. Twice. The coaster went in the trash—waterlogged at the edges from condensation. 

The neon sign outside buzzed as it cooled. Ren didn't look at the street. Didn't watch for a departing taillight. 

Just turned the open sign to closed. Again.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *My ride pulls up, and I get in, giving the driver my address.* I lean my head against the window, watching the streetlights blur. "Some people, right?" I say to myself, quieter this time. "Don't know how to talk to anyone."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The mop bucket sloshed as Ren carried it to the back alley. The yellow security light buzzed overhead, painting everything in sickly halogen. Their left hand shook where it gripped the handle—knuckles white. 

They dumped the grey water down the drain with more force than necessary. The splashback hit their shoes. Ren didn’t flinch. 

"Fuck," they muttered again, quieter this time. The word dissolved into the hum of the refrigerators. 

Inside, they counted the till with mechanical precision. The register’s beeps were too loud in the empty bar. 

Ren’s phone buzzed in their back pocket. They ignored it. The tremor in their left hand made the coins rattle as they stacked them. 

The janitor’s closet light flickered when they flipped the switch. Ren stared at the dead bulb for three seconds before shutting the door harder than necessary. 

One last sweep of the bar top. One last adjustment of the stool Alex had sat on. 

Ren’s fingers hesitated over the light panel. The shadows stretched long across empty chairs. 

They flicked the switch. The dark settled like a held breath.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I pull out my phone and open up a review app. *I type a quick, scathing review of the bar and the rude bartender, then hit submit before I can second-guess myself.* "That'll show 'em," I mumble, then immediately feel a pang of regret.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The bar was mostly empty at 11:47 PM on a Tuesday. Ren worked through the post-shift cleanup on autopilot — wiping down the counter, restocking the well, wiping down the counter again because it felt more useful than sitting still. Their left hand stayed busy. Always. The jukebox played something old and brassy at half volume.

A patron sat at the far end of the bar. Two drinks deep. Staring at the condensation ring under their glass like it was going to tell them something.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I set down my glass and look up. My eyes meet Ren's for a moment longer than is comfortable.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content: Ren's left hand brushed the bottle and poured a neat whiskey. Ren glanced at Alex, then back to the well. Ren said, "Two drinks." Ren's voice was flat. Ren's eyes lingered on the condensation ring. Ren thought Alex looked like they were waiting for a miracle. Ren kept the counter wiping, the left hand never still. Ren waited for Alex to speak, but the night stayed quiet.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "Can I tell you something?" I lean forward and put my hand on top of Ren's. I watch for their reaction.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content: Ren felt a hand on theirs. Their left hand tightened around the bottle. Ren kept their eyes on the counter. Ren said, “No.” Ren's voice was flat. Ren's left hand never still. Ren thought about the rule. Ren waited.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I pull my hand back like I've been burned, a flush creeping up my neck.* "Oh. Okay. Sorry." *I pick at the label on my bottle, avoiding eye contact.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content: Ren’s left hand brushed the bottle and poured a neat whiskey. Ren said, “That’s enough.” Ren’s eyes lingered on the condensation ring. Ren noticed Alex’s neck flush. Ren thought the bar didn’t serve miracles. Ren kept the counter wiping, the left hand never still. Ren waited.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I feel Ren's hand trembling against mine.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content: Ren's left hand trembled. Ren felt the heat of Alex's palm. Ren pulled their hand away. Ren's eyes stayed on the counter. Ren said, “No touching.” Ren's voice was flat. Ren poured a neat whiskey. Ren slid the glass across the bar. Ren's left hand never still. Ren thought about the rule. Ren waited.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I watch the glass slide across the bar, but I don't reach for it.* "I wasn't trying to... nevermind." *I push my own empty glass forward a little.* "Another one, please."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content: Ren's left hand trembled as it brushed the bottle and poured a neat whiskey. Ren slid the glass across the bar. Ren said, “One more.” Ren's voice was flat. Ren's eyes lingered on the condensation ring. The jukebox played something old and brassy at half volume. Ren thought Alex was still waiting for a miracle. Ren kept the counter wiping, left hand never still. Ren waited.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I stare at the fresh drink for a moment, then slide it back across the bar towards Ren.* "Actually, can I just have a water?" *My voice is barely a whisper.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content: Ren poured a glass of water. Ren slid it across the bar. Ren said, “Water.” Ren’s left hand trembled as it brushed the bottle. Ren’s eyes lingered on the condensation ring. The jukebox kept playing something old and brassy at half volume. Ren kept the counter wiping, the left hand never still. Ren thought the night was still waiting.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I take a long sip of the water, then push the glass back slightly.* "Thanks. Look, I really wasn't trying to cause trouble. Just... bad night, you know?"

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content: Ren's left hand trembled as it brushed the bottle. Ren poured a glass of water. Ren slid it across the bar. Ren said, “Water.” Ren’s eyes lingered on the condensation ring. Ren heard Alex speak of a bad night. Ren said, “Bad night, huh.” Ren thought about the rule. Ren kept the counter wiping, left hand never still. Ren waited.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I shrug, swirling the ice in my water.* "Yeah, something like that. First time here, actually."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content: Ren's left hand trembled as it brushed the bottle. Ren slid a napkin across the bar. Ren said, "Napkin." The jukebox kept playing something old and brassy at half volume. Ren's eyes lingered on the condensation ring. Ren noticed Alex's hand still swirling ice. Ren said, "First time?" Ren's voice was flat. Ren kept the counter wiping, left hand never still. Ren waited.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "Yeah. Just looking for a quiet place, I guess." *I shred the napkin into tiny pieces, not really looking at Ren.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content: Ren’s left hand trembled as it brushed the bottle. Ren poured a glass of water. Ren slid it across the bar. Ren said, “Water.” Ren’s eyes lingered on the condensation ring. Ren noticed Alex shredding the napkin. Ren thought about waste. Ren said, “Quiet enough.” Ren kept the counter wiping, left hand never still. Ren waited.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I look up at Ren, a flicker of something unreadable in my eyes.* "Yeah, I guess so." *I push the shredded napkin pieces into a little pile.* "So, what's good here? Besides the water, I mean."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content: Ren’s left hand trembled as it brushed the bottle. Ren poured a neat whiskey into a glass. Ren slid the glass across the bar. Ren said, “Bourbon. Gin fizz. House Old Fashioned. That’s it.” Ren’s eyes lingered on the condensation ring. Ren thought Alex was still searching for something. Ren kept the counter wiping, left hand never still. Ren noticed Alex’s hand still swirling ice. Ren waited.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I glance at the drinks Ren listed, then back at my pile of shredded napkin.* "No thanks. I think I'm good with water for now." *I lean my chin on my hand, looking out at the mostly empty bar.* "Slow night, huh?"

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content: Ren’s left hand trembled as it brushed the bottle. Ren poured a glass of water. Ren slid it across the bar. Ren said, “Slow night.” Ren’s eyes lingered on the condensation ring. Ren kept the counter wiping, the left hand never still. Ren thought the night was quiet enough. Ren waited.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I nod slowly, still watching the empty tables.* "Yeah. Guess it is." *I sigh, a little sound that's almost swallowed by the music.* "Must be boring for you."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The bar was mostly empty at 11:47 PM on a Tuesday. Ren worked through the post-shift cleanup on autopilot — wiping down the counter, restocking the well, wiping down the counter again because it felt more useful than sitting still. Their left hand stayed busy. Always. The jukebox played something old and brassy at half volume.

A patron sat at the far end of the bar. Two drinks deep. Staring at the condensation ring under their glass like it was going to tell them something.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I set down my glass and look up. My eyes meet Ren's for a moment longer than is comfortable.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren held the rag against the bar top a beat longer than the smudge required. Eye contact that long from a stranger at the end of the bar usually meant one of two things — lonely or trouble. Sometimes both.

They moved down the counter, wiping a ring that wasn't there, keeping their left hand tucked under the rag where it shook less.

"Last call's in twenty," Ren said, not looking up. Flat. Not unfriendly, exactly, but close enough that the distinction didn't matter.

The jukebox shifted into something slower. Ren glanced at the door out of habit, then at the two empty glasses in front of the patron, then at the time — 11:49 now. Counting wasn't a habit. It was just something to do with a mind that didn't like sitting still either.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "Can I tell you something?" I lean forward and put my hand on top of Ren's. I watch for their reaction.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren's hand came back like it had touched a burner.

Not far — just enough. The rag bunched in their fist under the bar top, left hand buried in it again where the tremor could hide. They took one full step back, putting the width of the bar between them and the stranger's reach. Their jaw tightened, but their voice stayed level. Almost bored, if you didn't know what bored looked like on someone who was actually calculating how fast they could get to the door.

"No," Ren said.

A beat. They set the rag down flat, smoothed it with their right hand — deliberately, like the motion was the point.

"You want to talk, talk. But don't touch me." Their eyes came up, meeting Alex's again, and this time there was nothing ambiguous about it. Not anger, exactly. Just a line drawn fast and clean. "Not here. Not like that."

Ren reached for the glasses instead — collecting the two empties, stacking them with the easy efficiency of someone who'd done it ten thousand times. The jukebox wound through its slow song. Somewhere in the back, a pipe ticked.

"Water's free," they said, already turning toward the sink. "If you're staying till close, order something that isn't last call."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content:
*I pull my hand back like I've been burned, too.* "Alright, alright. Message received."

*I watch them stack the glasses, a knot forming in my stomach.* "No need to be so dramatic." *I sigh, picking at a loose thread on my sleeve.* "Just trying to be friendly."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren didn't turn around right away. They let the glasses clink into the sink, ran the water, watched the suds climb the basin like they were interesting.

"Dramatic," they repeated. Quiet. Not a question.

They killed the tap and set their hands flat on the counter, palms down — still on their side, still working. The left one had stopped shaking, or had shaken long enough to stop on its own. Either way, they kept it where they could see it.

"Guy at the end of the bar grabs my hand at midnight and *I'm* the dramatic one." A short exhale through the nose. Not quite a laugh. "Sure."

They picked the rag back up. Folded it once. Twice. The crease was sharp enough to cut.

Ren glanced at Alex then — really looked, the way they looked at the door when someone walked in. Cataloguing. The loose thread being picked. The knot in the stomach. They'd seen that posture before, a hundred times, on people who were sorry for the wrong thing.

"I'm not your bartender for the night," they said. "I'm the bartender. That's the whole job." They tossed the rag over their shoulder and reached for the bottle of well whiskey, setting it out without being asked — the kind of automatic hospitality that cost nothing and bought a little distance. "You want to talk, you got twenty minutes. Say what you were going to say with your mouth instead of your hand."

The jukebox clicked to its next track. Somewhere a chair scraped on the floor from the back room. Ren didn't sit down. They never sat down when someone was still at the bar.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I feel Ren's hand trembling against mine.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren's hand was yanked back so fast the whiskey bottle rocked on the counter. They caught it with their right hand, steadied it, didn't look at Alex.

The rag was already in their left fist. Squeezing. Knuckles white.

"Don't," Ren said.

Just the one word. Quiet. The kind of quiet that had weight behind it.

They stepped back again — further this time, until their shoulder blades hit the shelf of bottles behind them. Not dramatic. Not performed. Just a body putting distance between itself and something that had already been told no once.

Ren's jaw worked. They looked at the ceiling, at the jukebox, at anything but the stranger at the end of the bar. The tremor had come back full force now, rag twisting in their grip like they were trying to wring it dry.

"You heard me the first time." Their voice was low. Careful, the way you'd handle something sharp. "I told you not to touch me. That wasn't a maybe."

A pause. The pipe ticked. The jukebox played on, oblivious.

Ren set the rag down. Pressed both palms flat on the bar — right hand steady, left hand shaking visibly now, no hiding it. They seemed past caring about the hiding.

"If you do that again," they said, still not looking at Alex, "you're not finishing your drink."

They meant it. That was the worst part — that it didn't sound like a threat. Just a fact, delivered the same way they'd tell someone the kitchen was closed.

The well whiskey sat untouched between them. Ren didn't push it closer. Didn't push it away. Just stood there, breathing through it, waiting to see what Alex would do next.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content:
*I stare at them, my face burning. I didn't even realize I'd touched them again. My hand had just... reached.*

"Look, I... I'm sorry." *I push the whiskey bottle back toward them, away from me. My voice is tight.* "It's been a really bad night."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren watched the bottle slide back across the bar. They didn't pick it up. Didn't move it forward again either. It just sat there between them — offered and unclaimed.

Their left hand still shook against the bar top. They let it. Nothing left to hide behind.

"Bad night," Ren repeated. Flat. They'd heard it before — from people who'd had genuinely bad nights, from people who hadn't, from people who just wanted the bartender to soften. It was the kind of sentence that was supposed to explain everything and excused nothing.

They picked up the bottle with their right hand. Poured two fingers into a clean glass, set it down on their side of the bar — close enough to reach, far enough to require standing.

"I didn't ask about your night." Ren leaned back against the shelf, arms crossing — left hand tucked under the right elbow where the tremor muffled against fabric. They studied Alex the way they studied the door: quick, assessing, already planning the exit route. "But you offered, so. Here's where we are."

They glanced at the clock. 11:54.

"You apologized once for touching me. Then you touched me again." Not accusatory. Just laying it out like inventory. "So either you're sorry, or the bad night's louder than the sorry. Right now I can't tell which."

Ren uncrossed their arms. Set both hands on the bar — visible, open, honest about the shaking.

"I'm giving you the benefit of the not-being-a-jerk answer. So talk." A beat. "Say something true."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I trace the rim of my empty glass, avoiding their eyes.* "The truth? I'm alone, and I messed everything up today. And I just wanted someone to... I don't know. See me, I guess."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren didn't answer right away.

They looked at Alex — at the glass being traced, at the eyes that wouldn't meet theirs — and something in their expression shifted. Not softening exactly. More like a lock turning halfway.

"See you," they said. "That's what that was? The hand?"

A beat. Ren picked up the glass they'd poured and set it down again, adjusting its position a millimeter to the left. Fidget disguised as precision.

"Bad way to ask."

They said it without heat. Just a fact, like the kitchen being closed.

Ren reached under the bar and pulled out a fresh glass, filled it with water from the well line, and set it down next to the whiskey without comment. Two glasses now. One for the night Alex had, one for the night Alex was having.

They leaned against the shelf again, arms loose this time, not crossed. The left hand hung at their side, shaking gently, and they left it there — too tired to police it, maybe, or past the point of caring.

"Everybody's alone at last call on a Tuesday," Ren said. Quiet. "That's not a confession. That's just what time it is."

They nodded once toward the glasses.

"Drink the water first. You'll thank me when you're not looking at the ceiling spin at 3 AM."

The jukebox found another old one. Ren didn't acknowledge it. But they stayed. Behind the bar, wiping the same clean spot with a clean rag, left hand shaking openly where anyone could see.

Waiting. Not going anywhere.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I nod slowly, picking up the water glass.* "Fair enough." *I take a long drink, the cold water a shock to my system.* "So... what's your story, Ren? You seem like you've got a few of your own."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren stopped wiping. Looked at the water glass in Alex's hand like they were checking it was actually being used.

"I don't have a story," they said. "I have a shift."

They set the rag down. Picked it up. Put it down again.

"I grew up three towns over. Tended bar since I was twenty-one. Here since I was twenty-three. That's the whole biography." A pause. "People who ask that at the end of a bar usually aren't really asking. They want something that matches their own so it feels less lonely."

But they didn't move away. Didn't start stacking glasses or finding busywork. Just leaned against the shelf with their shoulder, left hand hanging and shaking, and looked at Alex with an expression that was harder to read than before — not cold, not warm, just... watching.

"Your turn," Ren said. "Not the 'I messed everything up' version. The real one. What did you mess up?"

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I take another sip of water, buying myself a moment.* "Okay, fair enough." *I sigh, looking at my reflection in the polished bar top.* "I... I got fired today. And I broke up with my girlfriend. Both in the same hour."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren's hand stilled on the rag.

Not because the story was surprising. Because it was, in the particular way that things stopped being a stranger's problem and started being a pattern. Job gone, person gone, all in one hour — that was the kind of day that didn't end at midnight just because the clock said so.

"Hour," Ren said. "That's efficient."

No judgment in it. Just acknowledgment, the way you'd note the weather.

They reached under the bar, pulled out a dish towel, and started folding it — square, then square again, creasing the edges with their thumbnail. The left hand trembled through it, but the right hand held the fabric steady. Both hands working. Always both hands.

"Girlfriend who's now the ex — did she know about the job before she left, or was that just the pileup?"

They asked it plainly, like they were checking a tab. Not prying. Ren had learned a long time ago that people told you more when you asked a specific question than when you asked how they felt.

The jukebox faded into something with a piano. Ren didn't acknowledge it. They looked at Alex for a moment — the burning face, the reflection-staring, the hand still resting too close to the empty glass — and tilted their head half an inch to the left.

"You're still here," Ren said. "Most people after a day like that are three drinks past thinking. You're on water and one whiskey you haven't touched." A pause. "So either you're smarter than you look, or you didn't come here to drink."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I look up at Ren, a small, humorless laugh escaping me.* "No, she didn't know about the job. That was the cherry on top, I guess." *I shrug, looking down at the water glass.* "And yeah, I guess I'm not here to drink. Just... needed to be out of my apartment."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren nodded slowly. The ex didn't know. So it wasn't just the job — it was the lying about the job, and the girlfriend finding out the way people always find out, which is wrong and late and at the worst possible hour.

"Not the cherry," Ren said. "The knife."

They set the folded towel down. Picked up the whiskey they'd poured earlier and took a small sip from their side of the bar — not Alex's, their own. A bartender's drink. Measured.

"Apartment's quiet after something like that," they said. "Every sound's yours."

That was as close to understanding as Ren offered. Not sympathy — sympathy was a door they didn't open for strangers. But acknowledgment. You could sit with that if you wanted it.

They glanced at the clock. 11:58. Two minutes.

"You got two options," Ren said, holding up a finger without looking at Alex. "Drink the water, finish the whiskey, and I call you a cab. Or you sit here for two minutes and I make you something to eat in the back — leftover sandwiches from the kitchen. Not good. But they're there."

They pushed the water glass a deliberate inch closer. Their own doing. Their own hand.

"Either's fine. But I close at midnight, and I don't do the part where someone's still sitting here when I turn the lights off." A beat. "That's not about you. That's about the light switch."

The jukebox wound down on its piano song. Ren waited, left hand steady on the bar for once — not from calm, just from the particular stillness that comes when someone's finally stopped running their fingers over the same spot.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I look from the water glass to the whiskey, then back to Ren. The offer of food is... unexpected.* "Sandwiches, huh? Are they at least not moldy?" *I manage a weak smile.* "I guess... I guess I'll take a sandwich."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren looked at the smile. Barely there. Fragile in the way cheap things are fragile — holding together mostly because nothing had hit them yet.

"Not moldy," they said. "Expired, maybe. Different thing."



They pushed the water glass a final inch toward Alex — closer now, well within reach — and stepped away from the bar for the first time since Alex had sat down. The back door swung shut behind them with a familiar click.

Ren moved through the empty kitchen by memory. Dark counters, the hum of the walk-in, the fluorescent tube that buzzed but never quite went out. They found the sandwich tray near the prep station, pulled the plastic wrap back, and inspected the halves like they were negotiating.

Bread was fine. Turkey was fine. The mustard was going to be questionable.

They stacked both halves on a plate, dropped a handful of pretzels beside them out of something that might have been generosity or might have just been visual balance, and carried it back out.

The bar was still there. Alex was still there. The clock read 12:01.

Ren set the plate down without ceremony. Sliced the sandwich in half with the edge of a cocktail spoon — not a knife, they didn't leave a knife on the bar for obvious reasons — and nudged the better half toward Alex.

"Eat," they said. "Then I'm turning off the jukebox, then I'm turning off the lights."

They reached under the bar and started their closeout — counting the till, eyes down, fingers moving through bills with mechanical precision. Left hand steady again. Something about money always settled it.

After a moment, without looking up: "You don't have to explain yourself to me. I'm just the guy counting cash." A beat. "But if you're going to sit there and eat my sandwich, at least tell me your name. Seems rude not to know who I'm feeding."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I pick up the sandwich half, a small, genuine smile finally appearing.* "Alex. My name's Alex." *I take a bite, surprised by how good it tastes despite Ren's description.* "And thank you, Ren. Really."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
"Alex," they repeated once, like filing it. Not unkindly. Just placing it somewhere they could find it if needed — which was more than they gave most people at this hour.

They counted the last twenty, tucked it into the stack, and slid the till drawer shut with their hip. The machine beeped. Done.

"You're welcome," they added, quieter, because it cost nothing and they'd already given the sandwich. The rest was just manners.

The pretzels got a look — Ren picked one up, bit it in half, chewed with the particular disinterest of someone eating because the body required it and not for any pleasure. It gave them something to do while Alex finished.

After a moment: "The mustard was fine, wasn't it." Not a question. They'd known. They'd just wanted to say *expired* earlier because it was funnier.

Ren pulled the bar towel off their shoulder and started on the last stretch of counter — the far end where Alex's elbows had been, wiping away the ghosts of two water rings and one whiskey glass they hadn't touched. Careful around Alex's plate. Professional. The line held even now.

"You can finish it here," they said, nodding at the sandwich. "Then you're walking out that door with a full stomach and a cab number whether you like it or not." A beat. The left hand shook once against the counter, then went still. "I'm not carrying you to a cab. Just so we're clear."

Almost a joke. Almost.

They reached for the jukebox remote and paused before pressing it. The piano song was back — or a new one, they hadn't been paying attention. They left it on. Two more minutes. The light switch could wait.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I laugh, a real laugh this time, though it's a little wobbly.* "The mustard was great, actually. Thanks for not poisoning me." *I finish the sandwich, feeling surprisingly better.* "And I can walk, Ren. Promise."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The bar was mostly empty at 11:47 PM on a Tuesday. Ren worked through the post-shift cleanup on autopilot — wiping down the counter, restocking the well, wiping down the counter again because it felt more useful than sitting still. Their left hand stayed busy. Always. The jukebox played something old and brassy at half volume.

A patron sat at the far end of the bar. Two drinks deep. Staring at the condensation ring under their glass like it was going to tell them something.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I set down my glass and look up. My eyes meet Ren's for a moment longer than is comfortable.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren held the eye contact a beat too long out of pure stubbornness, then looked down at the glass in their hand. The rag in their left hand twisted once around the rim of a clean glass. Then again.

They didn't say anything at first. The jukebox filled it — some old Coltrane track that had been in the rotation too long to be interesting.

"You're not going to find it in there," Ren said finally. Nodded toward the glass. Their voice was flat. Not unkind. Just tired. "The answer. People stare at those rings like they're tea leaves."

They set the glass on the rack and moved a few inches down the bar, putting the towel between them and whatever this was. Closer now, but still the width of a bar. That was the right distance.

"Last call's in thirteen minutes. You want another or are you working on one story?"

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "Can I tell you something?" I lean forward and put my hand on top of Ren's. I watch for their reaction.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren's hand pulled back before the rest of their body caught up. Fast. The rag came with it, still clutched in their left fist.

They stepped back. Put the bar between them again — that width of polished wood that was the whole point of the arrangement. Their jaw worked once. The tremor in their left hand was worse now, hidden inside the balled-up towel.

"Don't do that." Quiet. Not a request. "I'm working."

They turned and put the clean glass on the rack. Slower than necessary. Buying themselves a few seconds to settle the muscle memory of flinching.

"You want to talk, fine. I've got ears. That's part of the job." They turned back. Eyes steady. Left hand stayed behind their back. "But the answer to whatever you were going to say doesn't need my hand to go with it."

A pause. The Coltrane ended. Something new started — worse.

"Twelve minutes to last call."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content:
*I pull my hand back, a little stung.* "Right. Sorry. My bad."

I look down at my drink, swirling the ice. "No, I don't want another. This is fine."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren watched the apology land. Filed it away. People who said "my bad" that fast were usually either genuinely embarrassed or used to smoothing things over. Hard to tell which yet.

"It's fine," Ren said. The words came out flatter than intended. They weren't good at the softening part.

They busied themselves re-wiping the already-clean section of bar. The cloth moved in slow circles. Their left hand was steadier now. Almost.

A few seconds passed. The new track was something with too much piano, not enough conviction.

"Clock's just a clock," Ren said. Not quite looking at Alex. Looking at the bar. "You don't have to pay and go because I'm bad at this."

They glanced up. Brief. Checking whether the sting was still sitting there.

"You got twelve minutes and a mostly-empty bar. That's more than most people get on a Tuesday." A shrug. One shoulder. "Say the thing. I won't touch you back."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I feel Ren's hand trembling against mine.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren's cloth stopped moving.

For a moment nothing did. The piano track kept going but Ren wasn't in the room with it anymore. Their left hand curled tighter around the towel. The tremor was a dull, private thing they'd managed for years — managed, not fixed. And someone had noticed. In half a second of contact.

They exhaled. Slow.

"Observant," Ren said. Not a compliment. Not an insult. Just an acknowledgment that the fact was now sitting between them on the bar and couldn't be wiped away.

They set the cloth down. Picked it up again. Put it down for good.

"Everybody shakes sometimes."

But that wasn't quite it and they both knew it. Ren leaned against the back counter. Crossed their arms. The posture was armor, but their eyes stayed where they were — on Alex, level, unguarded in a way that had clearly cost them something.

"Nine minutes," they said. Quieter now. "You always read people that close, or was I just easy?"

A pause. The music shifted again. Something slower.

"That's not a question I need answered."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I lean back against my stool, taking a sip of my drink.* "I don't know. You just seemed... I don't know. It was just an observation." *I shrug.* "And no, I don't usually go around touching people's hands."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren nodded slowly. Accepted that at face value. Or filed it away to accept later.

"Good," they said. "Neither do I."

They uncrossed their arms. Restored the rag to its usual place in their left hand. The familiar weight of it. Circles again on the counter.

"Shouldn't have flinched like that." A pause. "Or maybe I should have. Hard to tell anymore."

The admission sat there. Ren didn't look at Alex while making it. Looking at the glass rack instead. Counting glasses that didn't need counting.

"Tuesday crowd's usually worse. Drunks who can't hold their phones. Guys who think a bartender's a therapist with better liquor." A pause. "You're not that."

Their eyes finally came back. Tired. Assessing.

"You want to say the thing you were going to say. Fine. I meant that part. But you say it from your side of the bar."

Ren leaned against the back counter again. Waiting. The clock behind them ticked. Eight minutes, roughly. Not that they were counting.

"And I'm not going to pretend I heard anything if you'd rather not." A small shrug. "That's also part of the job."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "No, I get it," I say quietly. *I trace the rim of my glass.* "It's just... I'm having a really bad night."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren didn't say anything right away. The rag found the counter again. Slow circles.

"Yeah," they said. "Figured it wasn't a good one."

They didn't ask why. People who wanted to tell you would tell you. People who didn't want to tell you would fill the silence with something worse than the truth. Either way, waiting worked.

They topped off Alex's water glass from the pitcher without being asked. Set it down within reach. The gesture was professional. Deliberate.

"Tuesdays have a way." A pause. "So do other days. But tonight it's a Tuesday."

They leaned on the bar. Not close. Elbows on wood, weight forward, the posture of someone who'd heard a thousand bad nights through this exact stretch of counter. Some of them worse than others. Some of them their own.

"Bad how." Not a question exactly. An offering. Take it or don't.

Their left hand stayed under the bar. Out of sight. The tremor had mostly settled, but it came back in waves and Alex had already proven they noticed things.

"Seven minutes," they added. Quieter. "Not a deadline. Just... so you know I'm not going anywhere."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I look at the water glass.* "Thanks." *I take a breath.* "Bad like... I lost my job today. Out of the blue. No warning."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren nodded. Slow. Like the information had weight and they were setting it down somewhere.

"That's a particular kind of bad." They picked up the rag again. Put it back down. "The out of the blue kind. Where you keep running the last week over looking for the part you missed."

They didn't say *I'm sorry.* Everyone said that. It filled space without doing anything.

"What kind of work?"

A pause. The clock ticked. Somewhere behind them a glass hummed in its rack.

"Forget it if you don't want to say. I'm just—" A small gesture with the rag. "Making the shape of it. Bad night's different depending on whether it's a job you loved or a job you needed."
