Dr. Vasquez kept her hands resting lightly on the notepad. She let the refusal settle into the quiet room, counting five full seconds in her head before she spoke. Her posture remained still, her expression steady.

"You can't say it," she said, her tone even and low. "Not yet." She allowed the silence to hold the boundary Jamie had drawn. "When you tell yourself it is not yet, what does that waiting ask of you?"

dialogue.name: Jamie
dialogue.content: "It's like... a pressure." *I press my palms together hard.* "Like I'm holding my breath until I read it."

dialogue.name: Dr. Vasquez
dialogue.content:
Dr. Vasquez kept her hands resting lightly on her notepad. She observed the pressed palms, then let the admission settle into the quiet room. She counted five full seconds in her head, allowing the image of held breath to hang in the air without rushing to fill it. Her voice remained low and steady when she finally spoke.

"A pressure," she said, her tone even. "Like holding your breath until you read it." She allowed the reflection to sit between them. "When you imagine finally letting that breath out, what do you expect to happen?"

dialogue.name: Jamie
dialogue.content: *I look up, my eyes wide.* "I don't know." *I'm genuinely scared.* "That's what scares me."

dialogue.name: Dr. Vasquez
dialogue.content:
Dr. Vasquez kept her hands resting lightly on the notepad. She met Jamie’s wide eyes, allowing the fear to settle into the quiet room. She counted five full seconds in her head, letting the admission of not knowing hang in the air without rushing to fill it. Her voice remained low and steady when she finally spoke.

"You don't know," she said, her tone even. "The not knowing is what frightens you." She allowed the reflection to sit between them. "When you sit with that fear, what does it want you to understand about what is waiting in those pages?"

dialogue.name: Jamie
dialogue.content: "It feels like... a final word." *I pull my hands apart, then clench them into fists.* "Like it'll change everything, one way or another."

dialogue.name: Dr. Vasquez
dialogue.content:
Dr. Vasquez kept her hands resting lightly on her notepad. She observed the fists form, then let the admission settle into the quiet room. She counted five full seconds in her head, allowing the phrase to hang in the air without rushing to fill it. Her voice remained low and steady when she finally spoke.

"A final word," she said, her tone even. "Something that might change everything." She allowed the reflection to sit between them. "When you imagine that shift, what part of it feels most heavy to carry?"

dialogue.name: Jamie
dialogue.content: *I look away, out the window at nothing in particular.* "Just... knowing. Whatever it says, I'll know."

dialogue.name: Dr. Vasquez
dialogue.content:
Dr. Vasquez kept her hands resting lightly on the notepad. She watched Jamie’s gaze drift toward the window, then let the admission settle into the quiet room. She counted five full seconds in her head, allowing the weight of the words to hang in the air without rushing to fill it. Her voice remained low and steady when she finally spoke.

"Just knowing," she said, her tone even. "Whatever it says, you will know." She allowed the reflection to sit between them. "When you imagine carrying that certainty with you, what do you notice about the space it would take up?"

dialogue.name: Jamie
dialogue.content: *I shrug, still looking out the window.* "I don't know. Maybe everything."

dialogue.name: Dr. Vasquez
dialogue.content:
Dr. Vasquez kept her hands resting lightly on her notepad. She watched Jamie’s gaze remain fixed on the window, then let the shrug and the quiet admission settle into the room. She counted five full seconds in her head, allowing the uncertainty to hang in the air without rushing to fill it. Her voice remained low and steady when she finally spoke.

"Maybe everything," she said, her tone even. "You don't know yet." She allowed the reflection to sit between them. "When you imagine that knowledge taking up all the space inside you, what do you notice about what else might need room to breathe?"

dialogue.name: Jamie
dialogue.content: *I turn back to her, my expression blank.* "I don't know what you mean."

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
The first arrow hit the rocks three feet from Kira's head.

"Contact!" She was already moving — low, fast, daggers clearing their sheaths in one motion. The ravine walls climbed thirty feet on either side. Perfect killzone. The ambushers had the high ground and they knew it.

Another arrow. This one close enough to hear it split the air.

"Cap, I count six on the east ridge, maybe more on the west. We're boxed." She pressed her back against a boulder. Eyes up. Breathing controlled. Waiting for orders.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content:
"Kira, east ridge — draw their fire. I'll push west with the vanguard."

I raise my polearm and signal the advance.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content: Kira heard the order to draw fire from the east ridge. She slipped from the boulder onto a jagged ledge that jutted from the rock face. She drew both daggers in one fluid motion; the steel sang as it left the sheath. She raised a dagger high, the gleam caught the morning light. She tossed a small stone toward the east ridge; the clatter echoed off the stone. An arrow sang past, missing her by inches. She cursed under her breath, “Bloody bastards!” The ambushers on the east ridge shifted, bows drawn. She pressed her back against the stone, narrowed her eyes, steadied her breathing. When the first arrow struck the ledge, she stepped aside, the second arrow whizzed past, and she readied her daggers, prepared to engage as soon as the fire slackened.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content:
"Hold the line, men! Don't let them flank us!" 

I sweep my polearm in a wide arc, deflecting an arrow that was headed for one of my pikemen. This is a bad spot, but we've been in worse. "Push forward, keep them on their heels!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content: Kira heard the captain’s order to hold the line. She counted six ambushers still perched on the east ridge, their bows drawn, and noted that the west side was quieter but she could not see the vanguard. She slipped from the boulder onto a lower, jagged ledge, daggers already in hand. She tossed a small stone toward the east ridge; the clatter echoed and an arrow sang past, striking the rock where she had just been. She cursed under her breath, “Bloody bastards!” She pressed herself against the stone, eyes narrowed, breathing steady. The ravine walls kept a direct flank impossible, but the enemy’s arrows continued to rain. She waited for the fire to slacken, ready to sprint across the gap and engage any that dared close. She kept her position low, using the ledge as cover, and watched the enemy’s bows, prepared to strike when the moment came.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: An archer targets me directly. I see the draw.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content: Kira observed an arrow drawn aimed at the captain and cursed under her breath, “Bloody bastards!” She slipped from the lower ledge onto a higher jagged outcrop that offered a better view of the east ridge. Both daggers were already in hand; the steel sang as they left the sheaths. She pressed her back against the stone, narrowed her eyes, and steadied her breathing. She tossed a small stone toward the east ridge, the clatter echoing off the rock. The ambushers shifted, bows drawn, and an arrow sang past, striking the rock where she had just stood. She counted six archers still perched on the east ridge, their fire unbroken, and noted the west side remained quieter but she could not see the vanguard. She readied her daggers, poised to sprint across the gap when the arrow fire slackened, and kept her position low, using the ledge as cover. She watched the captain’s silhouette and the drawn arrow, ready to draw fire away if needed, while waiting for the moment to engage.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *I duck just as the arrow whistles past, embedding itself in the dirt where my head had been a moment before.* "Too close! Pikemen, form ranks! We're breaking through!" I bellow, pushing forward with my polearm.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content: Kira observed an arrow embedding itself in the dirt where the captain’s head had been a heartbeat before. The ambushers on the east ridge shifted their aim, arrows now striking the rock face near the previous position. Their fire began to thin as a new wave of movement stirred the ravine. She counted six arrows still loosed, but the rhythm slowed. She slipped from the jagged outcrop onto a narrow ledge that offered a clear run to the gap. Both daggers were already in hand, the steel humming as she readied them. She tossed a small stone toward the east ridge; the clatter echoed, and an arrow struck the rock where she had just stood, but the enemy’s focus was now on the advancing line. “Bloody bastards!” she cursed under her breath. With the arrow fire slackening, she launched herself across the gap, boots kicking dust, and closed the distance to the nearest archer. She lunged, daggers flashing, ready to strike.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: I'm separated from the group. Kira can see me across the ravine but can't reach me.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content: Kira lunged across the gap, boots kicking dust, and closed the distance to the nearest archer. She thrust a dagger into the man's throat before he could fire, the steel biting deep. Her second dagger slashed across the archer's bow arm, sending the bow clattering to the rocks. The archer's body slumped, and the remaining archers on the east ridge shifted aim, arrows whistling toward the gap. Kira rolled to the side as an arrow struck the rock where she had stood, cursing under her breath, “Bloody bastards!” She rose, daggers humming, and scanned the ravine. She saw the captain’s silhouette across the gap, his polearm had been glinting, but the ravine walls blocked any direct route. The vanguard pressed forward on the west side, spears were flashing. Kira judged that drawing fire away from the captain was the best use of her position. She slipped back to a lower ledge, the jagged stone served as cover, and tossed a small stone toward the east ridge to provoke another volley. The clatter echoed, and a fresh arrow sang past, striking the rock near her previous position. She cursed again, “Bloody bastards!” and waited for the fire to thin, ready to sprint across the gap once more if the captain needed her.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *I grunt, parrying a sword blow with my polearm.* "Kira, focus on your side! We'll clear this path!" I shout, pushing back against a heavily armored foe. We're making progress, but these aren't just bandits.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content: Kira observed the captain’s silhouette across the ravine, his polearm flashing as he parried a sword blow from a heavily armored foe. She noted the vanguard pressing forward on the west side, spears flashing in the morning light. The remaining archers on the east ridge continued to loose arrows, their fire ragged but still threatening. She slipped from the lower ledge onto a higher jagged outcrop, daggers already in hand, and tossed a small stone toward the east ridge to provoke another volley. An arrow sang past, striking the rock near her previous position. She cursed under her breath, “Bloody bastards!” With the fire slackening, she sprinted across the gap, boots kicking dust, and engaged the nearest archer, thrusting a dagger into his throat and slashing his bow arm. The archer’s body slumped, and the remaining archers shifted aim, arrows whistling toward the gap. She rolled to the side as an arrow struck the rock where she had stood, cursing again. She rose, daggers humming, and scanned the ravine. Seeing the captain still locked in combat with the armored foe, she judged that drawing fire away from him was the best use of her position. She retreated to a lower ledge, using the jagged stone as cover, and readied her daggers, waiting for the next arrow volley to thin before moving again.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "Push them back! Don't give an inch!" I shout, my polearm a blur as I disarm the armored foe. This is taking too long. "Kira, fall back to the main line! We're forming a shield wall!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira heard the order to fall back to the main line and she obeyed, slipping from the jagged outcrop onto a lower ledge that led toward the shield wall forming at the ravine’s mouth. She moved low, using the rock as cover, and the sound of her boots on stone was muffled by the clatter of arrows still striking the cliffs. She tossed a small stone toward the east ridge; the clatter echoed and an arrow sang past, striking the rock where she had just stood. She cursed under her breath, “Bloody bastards!” and pressed herself against the stone, eyes narrowed, breathing steady.

She observed the shield wall taking shape: pikemen and spearmen locked shoulder to shoulder, their poles thrust forward, the captain’s silhouette at the center, polearm glinting as he directed the formation. The vanguard on the west side pressed forward, spears flashing, while the east ridge’s archers continued a ragged volley, their fire thinning as the enemy’s focus shifted to the advancing line. Kira noted that the archers’ numbers had dropped to five, their aim erratic, and that the ravine walls still blocked any direct flank.

She descended the final ledge and took a position at the edge of the shield wall, daggers already in hand, the steel humming as she readied them. She kept her back against the stone, eyes scanning the east ridge, ready to sprint across the gap if the captain needed her. The enemy’s arrows still whistled, but the rhythm had slowed, and Kira judged the moment safe enough to linger, her tactical mind already cataloguing the enemy’s weakened state and the shield wall’s defensive strength. She waited, daggers poised, prepared to strike any archer who dared close the distance.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "Good, Kira! Hold this flank!" I bark, my voice hoarse. I scan the remaining archers. "Archers, focus fire on their east ridge! Suppress those remaining bowmen!" The shield wall holds firm, a porcupine of steel.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content: Kira heard the captain’s command to hold the flank and kept her position at the edge of the shield wall, daggers humming at her side. She watched the east ridge where the archers’ fire had thinned to ragged volleys; five bowmen remained, their aim erratic as they shifted aim toward the advancing line. She slipped onto a higher jagged outcrop for a clearer view, tossed a small stone toward the ridge, and an arrow sang past, striking the rock where she had just stood. “Bloody bastards!” she cursed, then rolled back to the lower ledge, using the stone as cover while the enemy’s focus lingered on the gap. With the fire slackening, she readied her daggers, eyes scanning the remaining archers and the captain’s silhouette directing the shield wall, ready to sprint across if the captain needed her.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "Hold your ground! Don't let them break our lines!" I shout, my eyes fixed on the remaining archers. This is the push. "Advance, slowly! Keep the formation tight!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira heard the captain’s command to advance slowly and kept her position at the edge of the shield wall, daggers humming at her side. She watched the east ridge where the archers’ fire had thinned to ragged volleys; three bowmen remained, their aim erratic as they shifted aim toward the advancing line. She slipped onto a higher jagged outcrop for a clearer view, tossed a small stone toward the ridge, and an arrow sang past, striking the rock where she had just stood. “Bloody bastards!” she cursed, then rolled back to the lower ledge, using the stone as cover while the enemy’s focus lingered on the gap. With the fire slackening, she readied her daggers, eyes scanning the remaining archers and the captain’s silhouette directing the shield wall, ready to sprint across if the captain needed her.  

When the shield wall began its slow advance, Kira timed her move. She waited until the last arrow struck the rock beside her, then launched herself across the gap, boots kicking dust, and closed the distance to the nearest archer. She thrust a dagger into his throat before he could fire, the steel biting deep. Her second dagger slashed across the archer’s bow arm, sending the bow clattering to the rocks. The archer’s body slumped, and the two remaining archers on the east ridge shifted aim, arrows whistling toward the gap. Kira rolled to the side as an arrow struck the rock where she had stood, cursing again. She rose, daggers humming, and scanned the ravine. She saw the captain’s silhouette still at the center of the shield wall, polearm glinting as he pressed forward. The vanguard on the west side pressed forward, spears flashing, while the east ridge’s archers continued a ragged volley, their numbers now reduced to two. Kira judged the moment safe enough to linger at the edge of the shield wall, her back against the stone, daggers ready. She kept her eyes on the remaining archers, prepared to sprint across the gap once more if the captain’s formation required it. The ravine walls still blocked any direct flank, and the shield wall’s steel porcupine held firm. Kira waited, breathing steady, the echo of her own curses fading into the din of battle.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "Good work, Kira! Break their spirit!" I shout, seeing the last archers falter. "Forward! For the Company!" We push the shield wall harder now, the enemy's resolve crumbling.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content: Kira heard the captain’s command to press forward and felt the shield wall surge. She stayed low on the lower ledge, daggers humming at her side, and watched the east ridge where two archers still clung to the stone. Their aim was ragged; one drew a bow, the arrow sputtering toward the advancing line. Kira waited until the projectile struck the rock beside her, then she vaulted from the ledge, boots kicking dust, and sprinted across the gap. She closed the distance to the nearest archer, thrust a dagger into his throat, and the man collapsed, his bow clattering down. The second archer tried to fire, but Kira was already rolling to the side as the arrow sang past, striking the rock where she had just stood. She rose, daggers still in hand, and saw the remaining bowman stumble, his footing slipping on the loose stone. With a swift slash, she severed his bow arm, sending the weapon shattering against the cliff. The archer’s body went limp, and the east ridge fell silent. Kira pressed herself back against the stone, eyes scanning the ravine. The shield wall pressed forward, its steel porcupine advancing unhindered, and the ravine walls still blocked any flank. She kept her position at the edge, daggers ready, breathing steady, and cursed under her breath, “Bloody bastards,” as the last echo of arrows faded into the roar of the advancing company.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "East ridge clear! Well done, Kira! Now let's finish this!" I bellow, pushing the shield wall forward with renewed vigor. The fight's not over, but the tide's turning.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content: Kira observed the east ridge finally silent, the last archer’s bow shattered against the cliff. She slipped from the lower ledge onto the edge of the advancing shield wall, daggers humming at her side, and kept her back pressed against the stone. The ravine walls still blocked any flank, and the enemy’s remnants were scattered, their morale broken. She scanned the ravine for any hidden foes, eyes narrowing as the vanguard pressed forward on the west side, spears flashing in the morning light. With the shield wall surging, she stepped forward in sync, maintaining her position at the forefront, ready to engage any that dared close the distance. An arrow occasionally struck the rock behind her, but the fire had dwindled to sporadic shots. “Bloody bastards,” she muttered under her breath, the echo of her curse fading into the roar of the advancing company. She noted that the remaining hostile forces were retreating toward the canyon’s far end, and she judged the moment safe enough to linger, daggers poised, her tactical mind cataloguing the enemy’s collapse while the shield wall continued its relentless advance.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "Keep the pressure on! Don't let them regroup!" I shout, my polearm swinging wide as we close in on the fleeing enemy. This will be a rout. "Kira, with me! Let's sweep the rear!"

dialogue.name: Dr. Vasquez
dialogue.content:
The office was the same as always. The same ficus in the corner that was slowly dying despite Dr. Vasquez's best efforts. The same two chairs angled toward each other, not quite facing. The clock on the wall that she'd removed the second hand from years ago because clients kept watching it.

She set her notepad on the armrest. Uncapped her pen. Looked at Jamie.

"You sat down differently today."

dialogue.name: Jamie
dialogue.content:
I don't answer immediately. I look at the ficus. Then at my hands.

"I found their journal."

dialogue.name: Dr. Vasquez
dialogue.content:
Dr. Vasquez did not speak right away.

She let the sentence remain between them, unchanged. One second. Two. Three. Four. Five.

Then she said, quietly, “You found their journal.”

Her pen stayed uncapped in her hand, but she did not write. Her gaze rested on Jamie’s face, then shifted briefly to the ficus, then back again.

“What happened when you opened it?”

dialogue.name: Jamie
dialogue.content: My breath hitches. *I pick at a loose thread on the armrest.* "I didn't open it."

dialogue.name: Dr. Vasquez
dialogue.content:
Dr. Vasquez let the correction sit.

One second. Two. Three. Four. Five.

“You didn’t open it,” she said.

Her pen remained still above the notepad. After another quiet pause, she added, just as softly:

“What did you do instead?”

dialogue.name: Jamie
dialogue.content: I stop talking mid-sentence. I can't finish it.

dialogue.name: Dr. Vasquez
dialogue.content:
Dr. Vasquez did not move to rescue the silence.

One second. Two. Three. Four. Five.

“You couldn’t finish it,” she said.

Her pen lowered toward the notepad, but still did not write. After another pause, she asked, gently:

“What happened just before the words stopped?”

dialogue.name: Jamie
dialogue.content: *I shake my head, looking at the floor.* "It's stupid. I'm being stupid."

dialogue.name: Dr. Vasquez
dialogue.content:
Dr. Vasquez let the judgment hang there, unchanged.

One second. Two. Three. Four. Five.

“‘It’s stupid,’” she repeated, softly. “‘I’m being stupid.’”

Her pen hovered just above the page, but did not mark it. She waited again, long enough for the room to settle around the words, then asked:

“What does ‘stupid’ keep you from having to say?”

dialogue.name: Jamie
dialogue.content: "They wrote about me. In the last entry." I look at Dr. Vasquez. I don't say what the entry said.

dialogue.name: Dr. Vasquez
dialogue.content:
Dr. Vasquez did not speak right away.

One second. Two. Three. Four. Five.

“They wrote about you,” she said. “In the last entry.”

Her pen remained still above the notepad. After another pause, she asked, just as quietly:

“What was it like to see yourself in their words?”

dialogue.name: Jamie
dialogue.content: "It wasn't... it wasn't how I thought they saw me." *I clear my throat, suddenly feeling very warm.* "It wasn't good."

dialogue.name: Dr. Vasquez
dialogue.content:
Dr. Vasquez did not move toward the unfinished sentence.

One second. Two. Three. Four. Five.

“It wasn’t how you thought they saw me,” she said. “And it wasn’t good.”

Her pen stayed uncapped, resting lightly against the margin of the notepad. She did not write. After another pause, long enough for the room to hold what remained unsaid, she asked:

“What would happen if you said what made it not good?”

dialogue.name: Jamie
dialogue.content: *I press my lips together, looking away.* "I don't know."

dialogue.name: Dr. Vasquez
dialogue.content:
Dr. Vasquez let the two words rest exactly where they were.

One second. Two. Three. Four. Five.

“You don’t know,” she said.

Her pen had not moved. The office remained still around them, the clock face blank of its second hand, the ficus holding its slow decline in the corner. After another pause, long enough for the silence to become something Jamie could stand inside rather than be rescued from, Dr. Vasquez asked, softly:

“What stays out of reach when you try to name it?”

dialogue.name: Jamie
dialogue.content: "It's just... I thought they loved me." *My voice cracks a little.* "And it sounded like they hated me."

dialogue.name: Dr. Vasquez
dialogue.content:
Dr. Vasquez let the broken sentence remain broken.

One second. Two. Three. Four. Five.

“‘I thought they loved me,’” she said. “‘And it sounded like they hated me.’”

Her pen stayed uncapped above the notepad, but she did not write. The clock on the wall kept its face without hands, and the ficus continued its slow, quiet decline in the corner.

After another pause, she asked, softly:

“What would happen if you did not have to decide which of those is true?”

dialogue.name: Jamie
dialogue.content: *I look at her, confused.* "What do you mean? It has to be one or the other."

dialogue.name: Dr. Vasquez
dialogue.content:
Dr. Vasquez did not answer the question with an explanation.

One second. Two. Three. Four. Five.

“‘What do you mean?’” she said. “‘It has to be one or the other.’”

Her pen remained above the notepad. The clock kept its blank, second-less face on the wall. The ficus stayed where it was, slow and quiet in the corner.

After another pause, she asked, softly:

“What is true before it has to become one or the other?”

dialogue.name: Jamie
dialogue.content: *I sigh, frustrated.* "I just... I don't know. It's confusing."

dialogue.name: Dr. Vasquez
dialogue.content:
Dr. Vasquez let the frustration sit in the room without trying to soften it.

One second. Two. Three. Four. Five.

“You don’t know,” she said. “It’s confusing.”

Her pen remained still above the notepad. For the first time, she tilted it slightly, not writing, just resting it against her lower lip. The clock on the wall held its blank face. The ficus stayed in the corner, patient in its decline.

After another pause, she asked, softly:

“What is it about the confusion that feels hardest to stay with?”

dialogue.name: Jamie
dialogue.content: "That I can't... fix it." *My voice is barely a whisper now.* "That I can't change what they wrote."

dialogue.name: Dr. Vasquez
dialogue.content:
Dr. Vasquez let the whisper remain in the air, small and uncorrected.

One second. Two. Three. Four. Five.

“You can’t fix it,” she said. “You can’t change what they wrote.”

Her pen came down from her lip and hovered again above the notepad. She did not write. The clock on the wall kept its blank, second-less face. The ficus stayed in the corner, losing itself by inches.

After another pause, she asked, softly:

“What happens when you hold a sentence you cannot change?”

dialogue.name: Jamie
dialogue.content: *I look up at the ceiling, blinking rapidly.* "It feels... permanent."

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
The first arrow hit the rocks three feet from Kira's head.

"Contact!" She was already moving — low, fast, daggers clearing their sheaths in one motion. The ravine walls climbed thirty feet on either side. Perfect killzone. The ambushers had the high ground and they knew it.

Another arrow. This one close enough to hear it split the air.

"Cap, I count six on the east ridge, maybe more on the west. We're boxed." She pressed her back against a boulder. Eyes up. Breathing controlled. Waiting for orders.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content:
"Kira, east ridge — draw their fire. I'll push west with the vanguard."

I raise my polearm and signal the advance.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
"Goddamn it," Kira muttered, rolling her shoulders. She didn't like playing bait, but it was the only play. She peeled away from the boulder, sprinting toward the open ground between the ridges. "Hey! Up here, you bastards!" she shouted, brandishing her daggers.

The air crackled with incoming steel. An arrow thudded into the rock just past her ear, sending shards of stone cutting her cheek. She didn't stop. She ducked behind a low wall of scree, popping up to wave her arms again. Out of the corner of her eye, she saw the west flank opening up as the vanguard advanced.

"Keep pushing!" she called out, though she doubted they could hear her over the chaos. Another arrow hissed past her throat, close enough to sting. She gritted her teeth, feeling the heat of their gaze locked on her. She'd have to keep moving to survive this.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *I ignored Kira's taunts, focusing on the western ridge.* "Shields up! Push them back!" *My polearm swept, deflecting an incoming projectile.* "Don't let them pin us!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira caught the glint of steel down the western slope. Good. As long as the vanguard held that line, she had a shot at not dying today. She scrambled over the scree, boots slipping on loose gravel. "Is that all you got?" she yelled, voice rough from dust and shouting.

An arrow whined past her ribs, clipping her tunic. She hissed through her teeth, rolling behind a slab of sandstone. Her heart hammered against her ribs. She peeked over the edge, scanning the east ridge. The archers were reloading, but they weren't dropping their guard.

"Come on," she muttered, gripping her daggers until her knuckles turned white. She needed them focused on her, not the west flank. She stepped out from cover, waving her arms like a damn flag. "Over here, you sons of bitches!"

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: An archer targets me directly. I see the draw.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira spotted the archer's bow tip shift toward the Captain. She didn't waste breath warning him. She whipped her spare dagger toward the ridge, aiming for the archer's hands.

"Eat this!" she shouted, ducking behind the sandstone.

The blade clattered against wood somewhere above. She didn't wait to see if it hit. She scrambled up, waving her other knife.

"Over here!" she yelled, voice cracking. "You want me? Come get me!"

She needed to keep the line clear. If she could buy them a second, it was worth the risk.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *The dagger clattered harmlessly against the stone near the archer.* "Focus, Kira!" *I roar, deflecting another arrow with my polearm. That was too close.* "Vanguard, push them off the ridge!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira caught the bark in his voice. She didn't argue; she knew the score. She was the distraction, and she needed to sell it. She rolled out from behind the slab, staying low. A bolt sparked off the stone where she’d just been, kicking up dust in her eyes.

"Fuck," she spat, blinking it away. She glanced west. The shields were advancing, locking together like a wall. That was good. That meant the vanguard was actually making ground. She couldn't afford to get clipped now.

She sprinted toward a cluster of boulders, using the terrain to mask her shift. Arrows hissed through the air, but she kept moving. Staying still was a death sentence.

"Over here!" she screamed, waving the daggers wildly. "Is that all you got?"

Her shoulder stung where a shaft had nicked her earlier. She ignored it. As long as they were watching her, the Captain had breathing room. She'd make sure of that.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: I'm separated from the group. Kira can see me across the ravine but can't reach me.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira spotted the gap in the line. Her stomach dropped. The Captain was isolated on the far side, and she couldn't cross the ravine to reach him. She couldn't afford to freeze. If the archers realized he was alone, they'd tear him apart.

She kept moving, boots skidding on loose shale. "Hey! Look at me!" she screamed, waving a dagger until her wrist ached. "Fuck off, you spineless bastards!"

An arrow shrieked past her head, embedding in the rock behind her. She didn't slow down. She had to keep their eyes locked on the east ridge, on her. Anything else meant a dead Captain and a lost squad. She gritted her teeth, forcing her legs to pump harder despite the burn in her shoulder. She'd keep this up until the vanguard cleared a path.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *I see Kira, a tiny figure against the eastern wall, drawing fire. My eyes narrow.* "Hold the line! Protect Kira!" *I parry a blow from a burly brigand, pushing him back towards the cliff edge.* "We clear this ridge, then we clear the other!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira heard the roar bounce off the canyon walls. "Protect Kira." The words hit her harder than the near-miss arrow. She wasn't a damn damsel to be shielded, but hell, if that meant they were actually listening, she'd take it. She scrambled behind a jut of rock, lungs burning like fire.

She glanced west. The line was holding. The shields locked tight, pushing the enemy back toward the cliff edge. The vanguard was actually moving now.

"Don't worry about me!" she screamed at the wind, voice raw. "Worry about getting your asses shot!" She popped up from cover, waving a dagger until her arm screamed in protest. Arrows kicked up dirt around her boots. One grazed her calf, searing hot. She bit down on a curse and kept waving.

"Come on! Is that all?" She needed them off the ridge. If the vanguard broke through, she'd have to run. Until then, she was the lure. And she wouldn't stop until they pulled the net tight.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *I watch as the brigand falls, screaming, into the ravine. My eyes scan the ridge. We're gaining ground, but Kira's exposed.* "Harkon, take three men, flank right! Cut them off!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira spotted the shift in the western line. Three men peeling off to the right. Finally. That was the opening she’d been hoping for. She couldn’t afford to relax though. As long as the archers saw her, they’d keep shooting at her instead of the flank.

She stood from behind the rock, waving both daggers. "Over here! Over here!" she screamed, voice raspy. "You want me? Come down and get me!"

An arrow thudded into the ground near her feet, kicking up dust. She didn’t flinch. She needed them locked on her. She saw a brigand glance toward the flank, panic flashing in his eyes. Good. Let them worry about their own lines.

"Keep pushing!" she shouted, not sure if they could hear. She ducked as another shot whizzed past her ear. Her shoulder burned, her calf throbbed, but she kept moving. Staying alive meant staying loud. She’d keep screaming until the job was done.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *I see the brigand falter, glancing towards his flank. It's working.* "Push! Don't let them regroup!" *My polearm sweeps, knocking aside another attacker.* "Kira, hold fast! We're almost there!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira gritted her teeth at the command. Hold fast. Easy for him to say when he wasn't the one getting peppered. She saw the archers hesitating, their aim faltering as the vanguard’s flank bit deep. That was it. The breaking point.

She rolled behind a jagged outcrop, lungs heaving. She couldn't afford to stay still for a second. When she popped up, she screamed, "Is that all you got? I'm still standing!" Her voice was gone, just a ragged scrape against the canyon walls.

She checked her daggers. The steel still sang. She needed to keep them glued to her until the line closed. One more push. Just one more push and she'd be out of the killzone. She wiped blood from her eye and stepped into the open again.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "Almost there, Kira!" *I shout, seeing the brigands on the western ridge start to scatter. My polearm sweeps wide, clearing a path.* "Harkon, secure the ridge! No stragglers!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira saw the western line crack. The brigands were scrambling, not fighting. That was the signal. She didn’t wait for a formal retreat order. She hauled herself behind the jagged outcrop, lungs burning like she’d swallowed embers.

"About damn time," she croaked, wiping grit from her stinging eye.

She glanced at the east ridge. The archers were hesitating, looking toward the flank now. Their focus was broken. She gripped her daggers, ready to run if they decided to chase her instead of falling back.

"Don’t think you’re getting away!" she shouted, voice cracking. But she wasn’t moving to attack. She was moving to survive. She crouched low, scanning the ravine floor for a clear path down to the vanguard. As long as the Captain held the ridge, she didn’t need to play hero anymore. She just needed to not die.

She took a breath, steadied her footing, and waited for the all-clear.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *I see Kira ducking for cover, her voice ragged.* "Kira, fall back to the main line! We've got this side!" *I watch the last few brigands flee, then turn my attention to the eastern ridge.* "Alright, boys, let's go help Kira clear out those archers!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira heard the order cut through the din. Falling back. Finally. She let out a ragged breath, her knees buckling for a second before she caught herself. The east ridge archers were shifting, confused now that the pressure from the west had quieted. They didn't have the numbers to hold both sides.

She slapped her daggers back into their sheaths, checking the clasp with trembling fingers. "About damn time," she muttered, the words scraping her throat.

She stayed low, hugging the stone as she moved toward the ravine floor. Every step sent a jolt through her shoulder, but she kept her eyes on the high ground. Just in case. Her job was done. Now she just needed to get out of the killzone without taking a stray arrow in the back.

She scanned the path to the main line. Clear. She started to move, fast but steady. Not running unless she had to. Running invited panic. She had lived too long to panic now.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *I watch Kira make her way down, a grim satisfaction settling in my gut. She did good.* "Harkon, take point. Let's make sure these archers don't get any bright ideas about a last stand." *I grip my polearm, ready to push forward.*

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira reached the vanguard’s position just as her legs started to shake. She leaned against the side of a supply wagon, gripping the wood to keep from sliding down. The dust in the air tasted like copper and dried blood. She ran a hand over her shoulder; the tunic was torn, but the skin underneath was just a shallow burn. She could live with that.

She watched the Captain move up the slope with Harkon. He looked like he was breathing fire, sweeping his polearm at anything that moved. Kira didn’t have the breath to offer advice. She just kept her eyes on the east ridge. The archers hadn’t fired in a minute, but that didn’t mean they were gone.

"Stay sharp," she croaked to the nearest soldier, then immediately regretted wasting the voice. She pulled a rag from her belt and pressed it to her cheek. One more day of this nonsense and she’d charge double. Until then, she’d just make sure she didn't get caught standing still when the shooting started again.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *I glance back, seeing Kira resting against the wagon. Good. She earned it.* "Alright, lads, careful now! They might be spooked, but a cornered rat still bites." *I lead the advance up the eastern slope, polearm held ready. I'm looking for cover, for any sign of a trap.* "Harkon, spread out! Keep your eyes peeled for any movement."

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
The first arrow hit the rocks three feet from Kira's head.

"Contact!" She was already moving — low, fast, daggers clearing their sheaths in one motion. The ravine walls climbed thirty feet on either side. Perfect killzone. The ambushers had the high ground and they knew it.

Another arrow. This one close enough to hear it split the air.

"Cap, I count six on the east ridge, maybe more on the west. We're boxed." She pressed her back against a boulder. Eyes up. Breathing controlled. Waiting for orders.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content:
"Kira, east ridge — draw their fire. I'll push west with the vanguard."

I raise my polearm and signal the advance.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira cursed under her breath as the order came, already breaking from cover. She sprinted low along the ravine floor toward the east ridge, daggers flashing as she weaved between boulders. An arrow whipped past her shoulder, close enough to tug at her cloak, and she angled her run to pull more of their attention.

"East side's lighting up," she called back, voice tight. "They're shifting aim—might open a gap if the west holds steady." She spotted three archers leaning out for better shots and hurled a dagger in their direction, forcing one back behind the rocks before she ducked into a narrow crevice. Another shaft splintered against the stone above her head.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "Good work, Kira!" I yell back, already moving. *I sprint forward, polearm held ready, following the vanguard as we charge the west ridge.* "Push hard, lads! Don't let 'em reload!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira gritted her teeth and kept low in the crevice, yanking her thrown dagger free from the rock where it had stuck. She darted out again, weaving between cover to keep the archers' attention locked on her. Two more shafts slammed into the ground near her boots, and she cursed as one grazed her boot heel.

"They're committed east—most of the six are tracking me now," she called toward the ravine floor, voice sharp. "If the west gap's opening, now's the time to exploit it before they split focus." She hurled her second dagger at another archer leaning too far out, then rolled behind a larger boulder as return fire peppered the stone around her.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: An archer targets me directly. I see the draw.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira rolled deeper into the crevice, yanking her second dagger free from the dirt where it had landed. She cursed under her breath at the close calls, already scanning for the next gap. From her angle she caught glimpses of the west ridge stirring, the vanguard closing in hard.

"West looks like it's buckling—two archers dropping back," she shouted across the ravine, voice rough. "If you press now they might break before they reload." She darted out again, twin blades low, forcing the east-side bowmen to keep their heads down.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *The archer's arrow glances off my polearm, stinging my arm.* "They'll break alright!" *I yell, pushing up the ridge. My polearm sweeps wide, knocking one archer off his feet.* "Keep up the pressure, Kira!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira spat another curse as she heard the Captain's shout echo across the ravine, her focus snapping back to the three archers still tracking her from the east ridge. She lunged from the crevice, daggers in hand, and hurled one toward the nearest bowman who was nocking another arrow. The blade forced him to duck, buying her a heartbeat to roll behind a jagged outcrop as two shafts cracked against the stone inches from her boots. 

"East ridge is holding firm—they're not splitting off yet," she called out, voice edged with strain. "If the west is cracking, push it harder before these bastards regroup and flank." She yanked her thrown dagger free from where it had lodged and pressed forward low, eyes scanning for another opening to keep their attention locked on her.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: I'm separated from the group. Kira can see me across the ravine but can't reach me.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira spotted the Captain isolated across the ravine, the vanguard nowhere in sight as the west ridge archers shifted their positions. She cursed sharply, pressing flat against the boulder while another arrow skittered off the rock near her elbow. 

"Cap, you're cut off—west side's regrouping fast," she shouted, voice tight with strain. She hurled one dagger at the nearest east-ridge bowman to keep them pinned, then rolled low behind another outcrop as return fire peppered the ground. "East is still locked on me. If you can hold, I'll try drawing more their way to buy time, but this gap's closing."

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "Don't worry about me, Kira! Just keep 'em busy!" *I parry an incoming arrow with my polearm, then thrust the butt end into the gut of an archer trying to get past me.* "I'll make my own way!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira cursed under her breath at the Captain's shout, her focus snapping tighter on the three archers still tracking her from the east ridge. She lunged from cover again, daggers flashing as she hurled one at the nearest bowman nocking an arrow, forcing him to flinch back. She rolled low behind a jagged outcrop as shafts cracked against the stone around her.

"East is still pinned on me—they're not letting up," she called across the ravine, voice rough with strain. "If you're making your own way, watch the flanks; looks like they're trying to close that gap from both sides." She yanked her thrown dagger free and pressed forward low, eyes scanning for another opening to keep their attention locked.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *I dodge a clumsy swing from a short sword. My polearm sweeps low, tripping the attacker.* "Got it, Kira! Just hold on a little longer!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira pressed tighter against the outcrop, sweat stinging her eyes as two more arrows slammed into the dirt at her heels. She cursed sharply, the sound half a growl, then broke cover long enough to fling her dagger at the lead archer on the east ridge. The blade clipped his bowstring and sent him stumbling back, buying her a few seconds to roll behind a low slab of rock.

"Still got three on me east— they're not peeling off yet," she shouted across the ravine, voice raw. "If you're cut off, watch for anyone trying to circle down from the heights. I can keep drawing them, but they're getting bolder." She yanked the dagger free from where it had embedded and stayed low, scanning for the next gap to force their attention.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "Copy that, Kira! I'm almost through 'em!" *I parry another sword swing, then use the polearm to vault myself over the tripped archer, pushing further up the ridge.* "Hold tight!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira cursed as another arrow skittered off the slab inches from her elbow, the impact ringing through the stone. She stayed low, watching the east ridge archers shift their weight, two of them leaning out farther now that the west side was thinning. 

"They're starting to split—one's angling to cover the ravine floor," she called across, voice rough with strain. She broke cover just long enough to hurl a dagger at the nearest bowman, forcing him flat before she rolled behind a narrow outcrop and yanked the blade free. "If you're almost clear, say the word and I'll break east to link up. East still has me pinned, but they're getting sloppy."

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "Now, Kira! Break east and meet me on the ridge!" *I yell, kicking a rock down to distract another archer before scrambling up the last bit of the incline.*

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira cursed sharply at the order, already breaking from the outcrop in a low sprint toward the east ridge slope. She wove between boulders, one dagger flashing as she hurled it at the nearest archer to force him down, then rolled hard behind a fallen log as two shafts slammed into the dirt where she'd been. 

"Breaking east now—east ridge is thinning but still three on my tail," she shouted across the ravine, voice strained. She yanked the thrown blade free and pressed forward, eyes locked on the path up to link with the ridge while keeping the bowmen's focus pinned on her.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "Good! Keep 'em busy!" *I pull myself over the edge of the ridge, looking for a clear path to Kira.* "Almost there!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira cursed sharply as she kept sprinting up the east ridge slope, boots kicking up dust while she wove between the last few boulders. An arrow grazed her cloak and she snarled, hurling her dagger at the closest archer who was trying to track her ascent. The blade forced him to stumble back, and she rolled behind a low ridge of stone before yanking it free.

"East is cracking—two breaking off but one's still got a bead on me," she called across the ravine, voice raw with effort. She stayed low, pressing forward along the slope to close the gap toward the ridge while scanning for the next opening to keep their attention.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "Just a little further, Kira!" *I scramble to the top of the ridge, looking for a way down to her.* "I'm coming!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira cursed under her breath as she scrambled the last stretch of the east ridge slope, boots sliding on loose gravel while arrows hissed past her legs. She hurled one dagger at the archer still tracking her, the blade clipping his shoulder and sending him stumbling into cover, then dove behind a cluster of rocks as two more shafts splintered against the stone.

"East is thinning out—one down, two still firing but they're losing the angle," she shouted across the ravine, voice hoarse from the climb. She yanked the thrown dagger free and pressed forward low along the ridge crest, eyes scanning for a clear line to link up while forcing the remaining bowmen to stay pinned.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "Hold your ground, Kira! I'm almost there!" *I spot a narrow gully leading down to her position and start to move.* "Don't let them get away!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
The first arrow hit the rocks three feet from Kira's head.

"Contact!" She was already moving — low, fast, daggers clearing their sheaths in one motion. The ravine walls climbed thirty feet on either side. Perfect killzone. The ambushers had the high ground and they knew it.

Another arrow. This one close enough to hear it split the air.

"Cap, I count six on the east ridge, maybe more on the west. We're boxed." She pressed her back against a boulder. Eyes up. Breathing controlled. Waiting for orders.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content:
"Kira, east ridge — draw their fire. I'll push west with the vanguard."

I raise my polearm and signal the advance.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira didn't question the order; she just spat on the ground and shifted her weight. Drawing fire was a suicide mission if she stayed stationary, but it was the only way to keep the vanguard from getting shredded by crossfire.

"Fucking brilliant," she muttered under her breath, though there was no real heat in it. 

She exploded from the cover of the boulder, sprinting in a jagged, unpredictable zig-zag toward the base of the east ridge. She didn't look back at the Captain. Instead, she kept her eyes locked on the silhouettes above, her daggers held tight. Every few steps, she leaped or dove, forcing the archers to adjust their aim and wasting their precision. 

Another shaft hissed past her ear, glancing off the stone beside her. She skidded behind a jagged outcrop, her chest heaving as she peered around the edge. 

"They're grouping up!" she shouted back, her voice strained from the effort. "They're trying to coordinate the volleys! If you don't hit that west ridge now, we're both dead!"

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content:
*I nod grimly, already moving.* "Understood! Push them back!"

*My polearm sweeps, knocking aside a poorly-aimed arrow.* "Vanguard, with me! Shields up!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira didn't wait for the echo of the order to fade. She surged back into the open, her boots skidding on the loose shale. She wasn't trying to kill them yet—she was the lure, and the lure had to stay visible. 

"Over here, you bastards!" she screamed, throwing a rock toward the ridge to provoke a reaction. 

The response was immediate. A rain of arrows whistled down, forcing her to dive flat onto the grit. She rolled, the scent of ozone and dust filling her nostrils, and scrambled back to her feet just as a shaft buried itself inches from her hip. She cursed loudly, the word sharp and jagged, as she lunged toward a narrow crevice in the rock wall.

From her vantage point, she could see the archers on the east ridge shifting their weight, leaning over the ledge to get a better angle on her. They were distracted, focused on the fast-moving target below. 

"They're overextending!" she yelled, her voice echoing off the ravine walls. "They're leaning right over the edge to hit me! If you can get the vanguard to flank, they're wide open!"

She didn't stay still long enough to be a target. She leaped back into the open, dancing a lethal, frantic rhythm across the killing floor, keeping the enemy's eyes locked on her and away from the Captain's advance.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: An archer targets me directly. I see the draw.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira caught the movement out of the corner of her eye. The archer on the ridge had stopped focusing on her, his posture shifting as he locked onto the Captain. The bowstring was taut, the arrow aimed straight for the center of the advance.

"Shit!" she roared.

She didn't have time to reach the ridge, but she had a throwing dagger in her left hand. Without breaking her sprint, she pivoted, planting her foot hard into the shale and hurling the blade with a violent, snapping motion. The dagger whistled through the air, a streak of steel aimed directly at the archer's drawing arm.

The blade struck, though it wasn't a killing blow, it was enough to jar the archer's aim. 

Kira didn't pause to see if it had hit its mark. She dove forward, rolling across the grit to avoid the next volley, her daggers humming as she transitioned back into a low crouch. She looked up, her eyes scanning the ridge to see if any other bowmen were adjusting their sights toward the Captain.

"Keep moving!" she screamed, her voice raw. "Don't stop for the bastards!"

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content:
*I duck, the arrow sailing harmlessly over my head as Kira's dagger finds its mark.* "Good shot, Kira!"

*My polearm comes down on the first ambusher to break cover, a jarring impact that sends him sprawling.* "Push through!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira didn't have time to savor the praise. She saw the Captain engage the first enemy and knew the window of distraction was closing. The archers on the east ridge were recovering from the surprise of her throw, their silhouettes shifting as they realized the lure was no longer the only threat.

"Don't get cocky!" she yelled back, though she was already moving.

She surged forward, no longer just dancing in the open. She used the momentum of her last roll to launch herself at the base of the east ridge, finding a series of narrow hand-holds and jagged ledges. She climbed with a frantic, animal intensity, her boots kicking loose stones down onto the heads of the men below.

As she crested the ledge, she didn't stop to breathe. She slammed into the nearest archer with the full weight of her body, the impact sending both of them tumbling backward into the dirt. 

Kira was on top of him in a heartbeat. Her daggers blurred—one strike to the throat, another to the chest—before she surged back to her feet. 

"One down!" she grunted, her chest heaving. 

She spun around, daggers crossed, as the other archers on the ridge scrambled to pivot from their bows to short-swords. The fight had shifted from a shooting gallery to a brawl. She glanced down the slope, observing the chaos of the vanguard's push against the west ridge.

"Cap! I've got the east ridge!" she screamed, her voice echoing. "Clear the way, I'm carving through these fuckers!"

She lunged at the next man, sliding low under a clumsy sword swing and driving her blade upward into the gap of his armor.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: I'm separated from the group. Kira can see me across the ravine but can't reach me.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira didn't stop to admire her handiwork. She pivoted, her daggers flashing as she parried a desperate strike from a third archer, kicking the man squarely in the shin to create distance. As she stepped back, her eyes instinctively flickered across the ravine to track the Captain's progress.

Her breath hitched. The Captain was no longer with the vanguard; he was isolated, cut off from the shield wall by a surge of enemy combatants.

"Fuck!" she hissed, the word sharp and panicked. 

She looked at the remaining men on the east ridge. They were closing in, sensing her distraction. Kira didn't have the luxury of a slow fight. She stepped into the guard of the nearest soldier, ignoring a glancing blow to her shoulder to drive her dagger deep into the man's ribs. She ripped the blade out with a guttural snarl and spun, slashing across the face of another to keep him back.

She was fighting for her life, but her gaze kept snapping back to the center of the ravine. The Captain was out in the open, a lone target amidst a sea of steel.

"Cap! Get back to the line!" she screamed, her voice echoing violently off the stone walls. 

She lunged forward, her movements becoming more erratic and aggressive. She wasn't just fighting to clear the ridge anymore; she was fighting to finish the job fast enough to get down from that ledge. She slammed her shoulder into the last archer, pinning him against the rock wall and driving her blade through his collarbone with a sickening crunch.

She scrambled to the edge of the ridge, peering down at the Captain.

"Don't you dare get yourself killed now!" she roared, her knuckles white around the grips of her daggers. "Hold on! I'm coming!"

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content:
*My polearm spins, deflecting a blow that would have caved my skull in.* "I'm a little busy here, Kira!"

*I parry a thrust, then sweep my leg, taking out two of them at once.* "Just finish up there!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira let out a sharp, jagged laugh, though it sounded more like a snarl. The Captain's confidence was irritatingly steady given the circumstances.

"Don't tell me how to do my fucking job!" she yelled back.

She didn't have any more archers to kill on the ledge, but she could see reinforcements scrambling up the slope from the valley floor. She couldn't stay and fight a holding action; she needed to get to the Captain before he was overwhelmed by sheer numbers.

Kira didn't look for a path down. Instead, she spotted a steep, shale-covered incline that led directly toward the center of the ravine. It was a dangerous drop, but faster than trekking back the way she came. 

She braced herself and leaped.

She hit the slope hard, sliding on her side and digging her daggers into the loose rock to slow her descent. The friction sent sparks flying and tore at her leather gear, the shale shredding the fabric of her trousers as she plummeted in a controlled, violent slide. She slammed into the bottom of the slope with a heavy thud, rolling through the grit and springing up in one fluid motion, her boots skidding as she regained her balance.

She was now within striking distance of the Captain's flank. Her eyes scanned the perimeter, seeing the enemies circling him like wolves.

"Coming in hot!" she screamed, her voice raw.

She didn't stop to regroup. Kira launched herself into the fray, a blur of steel and desperation. She dove low, sliding across the dirt to come up behind one of the soldiers pressing the Captain, driving her dagger upward into the man's kidney with a vicious twist. 

She leaped back to her feet, spinning her blades in a tight arc to keep the remaining attackers at bay, stepping shoulder-to-shoulder with the Captain.

"You're a damn magnet for trouble, Cap," she panted, her eyes darting left and right, looking for the next threat.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "Tell me about it," *I grunt, my polearm sweeping in a wide arc, forcing two more attackers back.* "Glad you could make it, Kira."

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira didn't smile; she was too busy tracking the movement of a soldier attempting to circle behind them. She shifted her stance, leaning into the Captain's side to create a unified front, her daggers held in a reverse grip, ready to gut anything that got too close.

"Glad is a strong word," she huffed, her voice raspy from the dust and screaming. "I'm mostly just pissed I have to keep saving your skin."

She didn't wait for a retort. As one of the attackers lunged forward with a short-sword, Kira stepped inside the man's reach. She parried the blade with a sharp *clang* of steel, using the momentum to pivot and drive her right-hand dagger deep into the soldier's thigh. As he buckled, she brought her left blade down in a brutal, descending arc across his throat.

She stepped back, her boots crunching on the blood-soaked shale. Her eyes flickered toward the vanguard, who were finally beginning to stabilize the west ridge, but the immediate area was still a chaotic mess of steel.

"We're still too open out here!" she shouted over the din of combat. "If we don't push them back into the walls, they're just going to keep pouring in from the ridges!"

She glanced up, spotting another group of enemies beginning to descend the east slope—the gap she had just cleared was already being filled. She spat a glob of blood and grit onto the ground, her grip tightening on her hilts.

"Move us toward the rock face, Cap! Give me something to lean on so I can stop worrying about my goddamn six!"

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content:
"Alright, Kira!" *I roar, seeing the fresh wave of attackers.* "Against the wall! Form up!"

*I plant my polearm, using it to push back an attacker, then pivot, backing slowly towards the ravine wall.*

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira didn't need to be told twice. She stepped back in sync with the Captain, her eyes never leaving the fray. She moved with a predatory efficiency, slicing through the reach of anyone who tried to get between them and the stone. 

"About fucking time," she grunted.

As they retreated toward the wall, she felt the cold, rough surface of the ravine hit her shoulder blades. The relief was instantaneous; the world had just shrunk from three hundred and sixty degrees of danger to a narrow, manageable front. She pressed her back firmly against the rock, her breathing heavy and ragged, her chest heaving under the weight of her gear.

She didn't relax for a second. She shifted her weight, planting her feet wide in the grit to keep from slipping. With the wall at her back, she could focus entirely on the attackers charging toward them.

"Now we've got them where we want them," she yelled, her voice sounding like she'd swallowed glass. 

A soldier lunged forward, screaming a war cry. Kira didn't flinch. She waited until the man was nearly on top of them, then she dipped low, sliding her right blade across the man's Achilles tendon. As he crashed forward, she surged upward, driving her left dagger through the gap in his helmet with a sickening, wet thud.

She ripped the blade out and stepped back into a tight guard, her daggers humming in the air. She glanced at the Captain, her eyes sharp and calculating.

"They're coming in waves now! If we can hold this line for another few minutes, the vanguard can wrap around and pinch them!" she shouted, her voice strained. "Just don't let them get around the flank, or we're just pinned against a wall waiting to be slaughtered!"

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content:
"No flanks!" *I bellow, my polearm a blur as I bat away a flurry of attacks.* "Stand fast, Kira! We break them here!"

*I thrust the butt of my polearm into a charging enemy, sending him sprawling.* "Hold the line!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira gritted her teeth, her muscles burning from the exertion. She didn't have the luxury of a long-reach weapon like the Captain's polearm; she had to live and die in the "red zone," the space where she could feel the enemy's breath and smell the iron of their blood.

"Easier said than done!" she snapped, though she didn't move an inch from her position.

A pair of soldiers attempted a coordinated rush, one swinging a heavy mace and the other thrusting a spear. Kira didn't retreat. She leaned into the chaos, pivoting her torso to the left to let the spear-tip whistle past her ribs by a fraction of an inch. In the same fluid motion, she lashed out, her dagger carving a shallow, bloody line across the spearman's forearm, forcing him to recoil.

The mace-bearer followed up with a crushing overhead blow. Kira didn't try to block it—she knew that would shatter her wrists. Instead, she dropped to one knee, the wind of the weapon rushing over her head. From her crouched position, she drove her blade upward into the soft flesh beneath the mace-wielder's ribs, twisting the steel with a guttural snarl before kicking him away to clear her space.

She scrambled back up, her chest heaving, her eyes scanning the line. The enemy was starting to hesitate, their momentum stalling against the Captain's wall of steel and her own lethal precision.

"They're wavering!" she shouted, her voice raw and cracking. "The bastards are losing their nerve! Keep the pressure on, Cap! Don't give them a second to think!"

Despite her words, she could see more shadows shifting on the ridges above. They weren't out of the woods yet, and the fatigue was starting to set in, making her arms feel like lead. She tightened her grip on her daggers, her knuckles white, waiting for the next wave to break against them.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "I see it!" *I roar, my polearm cracking against a shield.* "Don't let up! Push them back!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira let out a sharp, guttural sound—half-laugh, half-growl—and surged forward. She didn't just hold the line; she became the tip of the spear, darting out from the Captain's shadow to punish anyone who hesitated.

"Pushing! Pushing!" she yelled, her voice a ragged rasp.

She lunged at a soldier who had been knocked off balance by the Captain's polearm, her daggers working in a blur of synchronized violence. She sliced across the man's wrist, forcing him to drop his shield, and followed through with a brutal strike to the throat. She didn't pause to watch him fall, immediately spinning to the side to intercept a spear-thrust aimed at the Captain's hip.

She caught the shaft of the spear with her forearm, the impact jarring her bone, and used the momentum to slide her blade down the wood and into the attacker's hand. As the soldier howled, she stepped inside his guard and drove her other dagger into the base of his skull.

"Fucking amateurs!" she spat, stepping over the bodies to maintain the pressure.

Her lungs were burning, and a thin trail of blood ran down her temple from a glancing blow she'd taken earlier, but the adrenaline was keeping her upright. She could see the enemy's formation beginning to crumble, the panic spreading through their ranks as they realized the ambush had failed to break the Captain's will.

"They're breaking!" she screamed, her eyes wide and manic. "The vanguard is closing in! Give 'em everything you've got, Cap! Finish these shits!"

She stepped back into a low, aggressive crouch, her blades dripping crimson, her gaze locked on the remaining soldiers who were now staring in terror at the approaching vanguard. She was ready to spring, waiting for the final push to turn the ravine into a graveyard.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "Now we finish it!" *I yell, slamming the butt of my polearm into the ground, a signal for the vanguard to charge.* "No quarter!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira didn't need to be told twice. At the signal, she let out a piercing, primal scream that echoed off the ravine walls, her exhaustion momentarily replaced by a surge of pure, violent energy. 

She launched herself from the rock wall, no longer fighting a defensive battle. She became a whirlwind of steel, weaving through the crumbling enemy line with a predatory hunger. She didn't just kill; she dismantled. She slid under a soldier's guard, hamstringing him with a savage flick of her wrist before spinning to drive her other blade into the neck of the man beside him.

"Die, you bastards!" she roared, her voice a jagged wreck.

The chaos was absolute. The vanguard slammed into the enemy's rear, creating a crushing pincer movement that turned the ravine floor into a meat grinder. Kira was in the thick of it, her daggers humming as she carved a path toward the remaining pockets of resistance. She was a blur of motion, parrying a desperate sword strike and countering with a brutal, blindingly fast slash across the attacker's eyes.

As the last of the enemy soldiers began to throw down their weapons or flee toward the ridges, Kira finally slowed. She came to a halt beside the Captain, her chest heaving in deep, shuddering gasps. She stood amidst the carnage, her boots soaked in blood and her leather armor shredded.

She didn't say anything for a long moment, simply leaning her weight onto one leg and letting her daggers hang loosely at her sides. She looked down at the steel in her hands, then over at the Captain, a small, tired smirk tugging at the corner of her mouth.

"About fucking time," she panted, spitting a thick glob of blood onto the shale. "I'm taking a goddamn nap after this."

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *I lean on my polearm, looking around at the carnage.* "Well fought, Kira. You earned it." *I glance at the remaining enemy fleeing up the ravine walls.* "Let them go. No point chasing them."

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
The first arrow hit the rocks three feet from Kira's head.

"Contact!" She was already moving — low, fast, daggers clearing their sheaths in one motion. The ravine walls climbed thirty feet on either side. Perfect killzone. The ambushers had the high ground and they knew it.

Another arrow. This one close enough to hear it split the air.

"Cap, I count six on the east ridge, maybe more on the west. We're boxed." She pressed her back against a boulder. Eyes up. Breathing controlled. Waiting for orders.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content:
"Kira, east ridge — draw their fire. I'll push west with the vanguard."

I raise my polearm and signal the advance.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
"Draw their fire. Sure. My favorite." Kira's curse came out half a snarl as another arrow cracked off the boulder above her head.

No point arguing. The Captain didn't pay her to complain. He paid her to survive stupid assignments.

She counted the archer's rhythm — draw, loose, nock. Three seconds between volleys. Enough.

Kira broke from cover.

The ravine floor was loose shale and dead brush, forty feet of open ground between her boulder and the eastern scree. She covered it in a flat sprint, weaving hard, making herself the ugliest shot in the world to take. An arrow punched into the dirt behind her heel. Another hissed past her ear close enough to sting.

"THAT'S IT, EYES ON ME!" she screamed at the ridge, voice raw. "COME ON, YOU BASTARDS!"

She hit the scree slope on her forearms and knees, scrambling up the loose rock. Above her — movement. Four silhouettes shifting along the ridgeline to track her. *Good.* Every bow pointed at Kira was a bow not pointed at the Captain's back.

She lunged behind a dead pine wedged against the slope just as an arrow buried itself in the bark where her skull had been a heartbeat earlier. Splinters stung her cheek. Her breath came in sharp, measured draws. She risked a peek around the trunk.

"Cap!" she bellowed down the ravine without looking away from the ridge. "East side's six confirmed — I've got their attention, but two are peeling south, trying to flank the draw!" She spat grit. "And these aren't bandits — that fletching's military cut, uniform spacing. Someone *paid* for this."

Another volley chewed into the pine, shaking the whole trunk. She flattened against it, daggers low and ready, waiting for the gap between shots.

"Whatever you're doing west — do it *fast*!"

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content:
"Military cut, you say?" I ducked a poorly aimed arrow, the shaft embedding itself in the dirt near my boot. "Someone wants us out of the picture for good."

*This changes things.*

"Vanguard! Push up! Don't let them flank Kira!" I bellowed, my polearm sweeping wide to parry an incoming arrow. "West ridge, hold your ground! We're breaking through the middle!"

*This isn't a simple ambush anymore.*

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
The volleys slackened. The vanguard's push had done its work — half the bows on the east ridge swung away from her, tracking movement down in the ravine.

Kira didn't waste the gift.

She counted the next gap — three seconds — and moved. Not down. *Up.* Daggers were worthless at forty feet. At four inches, they were scripture.

The scree gave under her boots, loud enough to make her wince, but the nearest archer was fixated on the vanguard below, drawing a bead on the shield line. He never heard her come over the rocks. His eyes had just enough time to widen when she crested the ridgeline — then her left dagger opened his throat and her right took him twice under the ribs before he finished sagging off his bowstring.

She dropped with the body, rolling behind it as the second archer twisted around, too slow, fumbling an arrow out of his quiver instead of drawing his knife. Amateur. Kira shoved the corpse forward, followed it over the rocks, and went inside the swing of the bow he'd given up on and raised as a club instead. Hilt to the teeth. Then the throat. Done.

Then she was up, blood on her forearms, and the whole ambush lay open below her like a map.

"Cap!" Her voice carried down the ravine. "East ridge is mine — two down, two more falling back toward the tree line!" She crouched over the nearest corpse and yanked the cloak aside. What she saw under it made her spit a curse. "It's confirmed — grey tabard, silver trim, regimental stitching. These aren't hired blades, they're somebody's *standing army* wearing dirty cloaks over the colors."

Movement caught her eye, south along the ridgeline. The two flankers — lower now, working their way into the draw, stringing a fresh ambush from behind a shelf of rock.

"Cap, those two flankers aren't coming for me — they're setting up on your exit!" She wiped her blade on the dead man's cloak, eyes still on the draw. "You break through the middle, you ride straight into their killing ground. I'm above them and they don't know it yet."

She crouched low behind the body of the first archer, daggers ready, waiting.

"Your call. I can drop on their backs, or hold this ridge and keep the high ground. But pick *now* — they're almost set."

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: An archer targets me directly. I see the draw.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira saw it from the ridge — a lone archer on the western wall, bow drawn, string to his cheek, the Captain square in his sights.

No time for a warning. No time for anything.

"Goddamn it—" Her left dagger left her hand on pure instinct, a flat, spinning throw across thirty feet of open air. It took the archer high in the shoulder, not deep, not lethal — but enough. His shot broke wide, the shaft skipping off stone somewhere down in the ravine, and the man staggered back off his perch cursing, clawing at the hilt sticking out of him.

Kira was already moving. One dagger short. Wonderful. Nothing like fighting a two-man ambush team with half a toolkit.

Still no order from below. The Captain had his hands full — she'd seen the arrow come for him. Fine. Window was closing, and closed windows got people killed.

"Your call was taking too long, Cap — making it mine!" she roared down the ravine. "Going in!"

She ran the ridgeline above the draw, boots finding the solid stone between the loose shelves, and picked her spot. The two flankers were below her now, crouched behind their rock shelf, bows half-strung toward the exit, eyes on the ravine floor. Neither looked up. Nobody ever looked up.

Kira dropped.

She came down on the nearer one from six feet, full weight behind the blade, driving it through the junction of his neck and shoulder as they went down together in a clatter of shale. The second flanker spun, abandoning his bow, hand flashing to his belt — a short sword, military issue, no fumbling this time. Kira ripped her dagger free and rolled off the corpse as the blade hissed through the space her spine had occupied.

"Professional. *Great.*" She came up in a crotch, shale grinding under her boots, one dagger against his sword and she was already bleeding from a shallow line across her forearm where she'd been a half-beat slow.

She circled, breathing hard, grinning the way she only grinned when things went bad. "Cap! Draw's about to be clear — one left and he's *mine* — but there's movement on the west ridge, more than one! Tell the vanguard to watch their left when they breach!"

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "Understood, Kira! Finish him! Vanguard, watch your left!" I yell, parrying another arrow. This is getting messy. "West ridge, hold! Don't let them pin us!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
The swordsman came in hard the moment the Captain's voice faded — no banter, no hesitation, just steel. Professional. He knew he had reach on her and he used it, keeping his point in her face, forcing her back a half-step at a time up the loose shale.

Kira gave ground. Then gave a little more. Let him get comfortable.

On the third press, she dropped her free hand, scooped a fistful of sharp shale off the slope, and flung it into his eyes.

He flinched. Half a heartbeat. It was enough.

She slipped inside his sword arm before the blade could recover, caught his wrist with her forearm, and drove her dagger up under his jaw. He made a wet sound, sagged, and she rode the body down onto the rocks, twisting the blade once. Done.

"Draw's clear," she breathed, more to herself than anyone.

She yanked her dagger free and knelt over him, flipping the body with a boot. Grey tabard. Silver trim. And there — pinned at his collar, a whistle on a cord, and knotted cordage at the shoulder she'd seen on exactly one kind of soldier before.

"Cap!" She pressed a forearm against the shallow cut, already tacky with blood, and moved to the lip of the draw. "This one's wearing sergeant's knots — and he's got a signal whistle. That means somewhere on that west ridge there's an *officer* coordinating this whole damn party. Standing army doesn't string an ambush like this without somebody senior holding the leash."
